### 2.2.5.16 The signal circuit of knock sensor is faulty
`geely_coolray_en_838f12e4` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/d10ed96b1df73d5e48aa44715130a6c61009ef15b3c1da7de71d2b06d0819551.webp)

The feedback signal of the knock sensor to the engine control module enables the engine control module to control the ignition timing to the optimal state and the ignition system to achieve the best performance, and also prevents the engine from being damaged by the potential knock. The knock sensor is located on the cylinder block under the intake manifold. The AC signal voltage generated by the knock sensor changes with the vibration level of the engine during operation. The engine control module adjusts the ignition timing based on the amplitude and frequency of the knock sensor signal. The engine control module receives signals from terminals 1 and 2 of the knock sensor harness connector EN40n through terminals 46 and 47 of harness connector EN01.

### 2.2.5.22 Intake VVT solenoid valve control circuit fault
`geely_coolray_en_5f07980d` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/7d2e1688e54ea555e4debf94ac647c62152da6e3a7052a2d9928ab5da9f38559.webp)

The intake CMP actuator is connected to the intake camshaft and operated under hydraulic pressure. The hydraulic pressure is provided by the fuel pump to change the angle of the intake camshaft relative to the crankshaft. The operating power of the intake VVT solenoid valve is provided by the main relay, and the engine control module controls the grounding with a pulse width modulation signal. Thus controlling the flow rate of engine oil to the CMP actuator. The engine oil pressure activates a relief valve spool in the CMP actuator mechanism that is fixed in the front of the camshaft. When the relief valve spool acts, engine oil is introduced into the CMP actuator to rotate the camshaft.

The engine control module controls the internal grounding of the solenoid valve through the terminal 41 of the engine control module harness connector CA21a. There is a feedback circuit inside the engine control module. The engine control module monitors the feedback signal to determine whether the control circuit is open, shorted to ground or shorted to voltage. This DTC is set if the engine control module detects that the control circuit voltage is within a predetermined range when the control circuit is disconnected by commands.

### 2.2.5.23 Signal circuit fault of intake camshaft phase sensor
`geely_coolray_en_93339221` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/5f4b24f1d38ee3d155378724650bb0f2eee32beb538075af99b9607d9b18edc3.webp)

The engine control module uses the pulse signals of the crankshaft position sensor and the camshaft position sensor to monitor the correlation between the crankshaft position and the camshaft position. When the crankshaft rotates, it drives the speed sensor signal wheel to rotate together, and the teeth on the signal wheel will cut the magnetic line of the sensor. The change of magnetic flux leads to signal voltage output of a certain frequency at both ends of the sensor coil. The output signal is sent to the engine control module. The output signal represents the speed and position of the crankshaft. The camshaft position sensor is installed at the rear right side of the cylinder head. When the crankshaft rotates, it drives the camshaft and the signal wheel on the camshaft to rotate together through the timing chain. The crankshaft rotates two cycles and the camshaft rotates one cycle correspondingly, and the camshaft position sensor generates voltage to the engine control module under the action of the signal wheel.

2.2.5.24 Temperature signal failure of air intake pressure temperature sensor

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/ebd52c8706d2de265824f55762fa0fa7f5abf634f4091a4e7dc2e242785ec88d.webp)

The air intake pressure/temperature sensor is used to measure the air intake temperature of the engine and indirectly measure the air intake flow of the engine. The engine control module provides a 5V voltage to terminal 3 of the air intake pressure/temperature sensor harness connector EN34n through harness connector EN01n terminal 3, and provides the internal low reference voltage circuit of the engine control module to the air intake pressure/temperature sensor connector EN34n terminal 1 through terminal 9 of EN01 n. The engine control module will always record the length of time during which the starting switch is turned off. If the off time reaches the set time when the starting switch is turned on, the engine control module will calculate the temperature difference between the engine coolant temperature and the intake air temperature to determine whether the difference between the two temperatures is within the normal operating range.

### 2.2.5.28 Engine coolant temperature sensor signal circuit fault
`geely_coolray_en_2e324036` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/e39d4308ea90484c88423a56685dff664fdcba621ff405acb3a3416666d7bb11.webp)

The engine coolant temperature sensor is a variable resistance with a negative temperature coefficient, which is used to measure the engine coolant temperature. The engine control module will always record the length of time during which the starting switch is turned off. If the off time reaches the set time when the starting switch is turned on, the engine control module will calculate the temperature difference between the engine coolant temperature and the intake air temperature to determine whether the difference between the two temperatures is within the normal operating range.

### 2.2.5.30 Exhaust VVT solenoid valve control circuit fault
`geely_coolray_en_de7fdc21` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/cc856081a327bd30f25e316f0335303bb9a82747d38615e74863c9c3727cb359.webp)

The exhaust CMP actuator is connected to the exhaust camshaft and operated under hydraulic pressure. The hydraulic pressure is provided by the fuel pump to change the angle of the exhaust camshaft relative to the crankshaft. The operating power of the exhaust VVT solenoid valve is provided by the main relay, and the engine control module controls the grounding with a pulse width modulation signal. Thus controlling the flow rate of engine oil to the CMP actuator. The engine oil pressure activates a relief valve spool in the CMP actuator mechanism that is fixed in the front of the camshaft. When the relief valve spool acts, engine oil is introduced into the CMP actuator to rotate the camshaft.

The engine control module controls the internal grounding of the solenoid valve through the terminal 40 of the engine control module harness connector CA21a. There a feedback circuit inside the engine control module. The engine control module monitors the feedback signal to determine whether the control circuit is open, shorted to ground or shorted to voltage. This DTC is set if the engine control module detects that the control circuit voltage is within a predetermined range when the control circuit is disconnected by commands.

### 2.2.5.31 Signal circuit fault of exhaust camshaft phase sensor
`geely_coolray_en_c9dfaa5a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/ef42f6dea74296ba93d76d699a05101e0feacccc0218f9f56fdc597b04ecc13a.webp)

The engine control module uses the pulse signals of the crankshaft position sensor and the camshaft position sensor to monitor the correlation between the crankshaft position and the camshaft position. When the crankshaft rotates, it drives the speed sensor signal wheel to rotate together, and the teeth on the signal wheel will cut the magnetic line of the sensor. The change of magnetic flux leads to signal voltage output of a certain frequency at both ends of the sensor coil. The output signal is sent to the engine control module. The output signal represents the speed and position of the crankshaft. The camshaft position sensor is installed at the rear right side of the cylinder head. When the crankshaft rotates, it drives the camshaft and the signal wheel on the camshaft to rotate together through the timing chain. The crankshaft rotates two cycles and the camshaft rotates one cycle correspondingly, and the camshaft position sensor generates voltage to the engine control module under the action of the signal wheel.

2. Trouble code setting and trouble location:

![](images/fd1067f871425f31118f5bbb23b4a56bfccd07f89b086c8432e55aa0cb4b3597.webp)

3. Circuit schematic:

![](images/de3a27947c19f6b0a15ec7ad0036e41448c1db3a0d4298dccb6c60839660af35.webp)

### 2.2.5.34 Signal loop fault of crankshaft position sensor
`geely_coolray_en_63af582f` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/76d4e0775fc79d8ec8b6da1da6cf815a789312d4d391010585d6a22b7aaee29c.webp)

The working principle of the crankshaft position sensor is to make use of the magnetism effect. When the crankshaft rotates, it drives the sensor signal wheel to rotate together, and the teeth of the sensor signal wheel will cut the magnetic line of the sensor. The change of magnetic flux causes a certain frequency of output voltage to be generated at both ends of the sensor coil, which is output to the electronic controller. The output signal can represents the speed and position of the crankshaft. The engine control module can calculate the ignition timing, fuel injection timing and knock ignition control based on the input signals of the crankshaft position sensor and the camshaft position sensor. The crankshaft position sensor is also used to detect misfire and tachometer display. The engine control module uses the CAN network to transmit engine speed signals to the instrument.

Step 1 Use diagnostic apparatus to read the trouble code.

A. Connect the diagnostic apparatus to the DLC.
B. Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "ON".
C. Start the engine and run at idle speed for at least 5min.
D. Road test for at least 10min.
E. Read the trouble code of the control system to confirm whether the system has output a DTC.

![](images/8d4b9336bdf585a433dfa3cac0186c75a9267990b1a831c9aefb1a990ff2f421.webp)

Yes

![](images/c2fef612c1a1c56df6462b062b2b7a98734934e51a4a5956ed0e7cd6685e2513.webp)

A. Check whether prescribed fuel is used by vehicle.
B. Check fuel injector and ignition coil harness connector and related lines of each cylinder for damage, poor contact, aging, loosening, etc.
C. Check the air intake system for air leakage, etc.
D. Confirm whether the above items are normal.

Repair or replace the faulty part.

Yes

Step 3 Check ignition coils of each cylinder.

A. Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "OFF".
B. Remove ignition coils of each cylinder, and check whether ignition coils of each cylinder are normal.
C Use ignition coils of same model to replace the ignition coils of each cylinder respectively.
D. Connect the scan tool.
E. Start the engine and run at idle speed for at least 5min.
F. Road test for at least 10min.
G. Read the fault code of control system to check whether the fault code is output again.

System is normal.

Step 4 Check spark plug of each cylinder.

A. Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "OFF".
B. Remove spark plugs of each cylinder, and check whether spark plugs of each cylinder are normal.
C. Use spark plugs of same model to replace the spark plugs of each cylinder respectively.
D. Connect the scan tool.
E. Start the engine and run at idle speed for at least 5min.
F. Road test for at least 10min.
G. Read the fault code of control system to check whether the fault code is output again.

![](images/9a28bd942b70281e9f6edd52d324151f0ee94109e140808c474106637e10e590.webp)

Step 5 Check whether the pressure of each cylinder is normal.

A. Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "OFF".
B. Remove ignition coil of each cylinder.
C. Remove spark plug of each cylinder.
D. Connect cylinder pressure gauge to measure pressure of each cylinder.
E. Check whether the pressure of each cylinder is normal.

No

Repair pressure problems of each cylinder.

Yes Step 6 Check whether the injector of each cylinder is clogged.

A. Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "OFF".
B. Remove the injector of each cylinder.
C. Check fuel injector of each cylinder for clogging, poor atomization, etc.

No

Clean the fuel injector of each cylinder. Replace injector of each cylinder if necessary.

Step 7 Check the control circuits of injectors.

D. Check the ignition coil circuit of cylinder 4, refer to Ignition coil control circuit fault of cylinder 4

Repair the ignition coil circuits of each No cylinder for the faults. Replace harness if necessary.

Yes

2.2.5.55 Temperature signal fault of boost pressure/temperature sensor

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/ded317652b322060bf2684730bda9b35efc1e76e84f0d98608f331cc169109d3.webp)

The boost pressure/temperature sensor is located at the outlet of intercooler. The pressure sensor is integrated with the temperature sensor. The engine control module measures the boost pressure and the air intake temperature between the turbocharger and the throttle body through the sensor. The boost pressure sensor includes the following circuits:

– 5V reference voltage (Pin No.3) – Low-level reference voltage (Pin No.1) – Air intake pressure sensor signal (Pin No.4) – Air intake temperature sensor signal (Pin No.2)

### 2.2.5.59 Main relay control circuit fault
`geely_coolray_en_04ec11ba` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/a2c056d6fbc258a881756cf11fee251bab68e70466e257bbb537da93364c9ea8.webp)

The main relay is used to supply power to ignition coil, fuel injection nozzle, sensor and other vehicle components. The engine control module harness connector CA21a terminal M2 controls the suction of main relay. There is a detection circuit inside the engine control module The engine control module monitors the feedback voltage to determine whether the control circuit is open, shorted to ground or shorted to power supply.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_2065db08` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before performing these steps, observe the data list of the diagnostic apparatus and analyze the accuracy of each data, which helps to quickly remove the trouble!

![](images/76b3fff7ec1a91c2b48c414077487dbaece76f62ac8d1d4a1a84f507fc30b0bc.webp)

A. Connect the scan tool.
B. Start the engine and turn on the scan tool.
C. Keep the engine speed at about 2,500 rpm to warm up for more than two minutes, and measure the oxygen sensor at idle speed so that its working temperature can reach 350℃.
D. Select on the diagnostic apparatus: engine/read data stream/front oxygen sensor voltage.
E. Observe the output voltage of the front oxygen sensor. The data stream should fluctuate within the range of 0.1-0.9V.
F. If the data flow shows that the voltage continues to be below 0.45V (mixed gas is too lean), perform the check steps as follows: • Inject proper amount of propane gas into the air inlet. • Observe whether the data flow voltage of the front oxygen sensor changes significantly, and the signal voltage will increase rapidly.
G. If the data stream shows that the voltage continues to be higher than 0.45V (mixed gas is too dense), perform the check steps as follows: • -Put the transmission gear in Neutral or Park gear. • Tighten the hand brake. • Depress the accelerator pedal to suddenly increase the engine speed to 4,000rpm and then quickly release it. • Repeat the previous step 3 times or more. Observe whether the data stream voltage of the front oxygen sensor changes significantly, and whether the signal voltage decreases rapidly.
H. When performing the above test, the signal voltage of the oxygen sensor should change significantly.

Refer to Replacement of oxygen sensor

### 2.2.5.69 Self-learning fault of electronic throttle
`geely_coolray_en_ae16f780` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/2fc26901186dfac6809f5713440d832340ec581722a21275afa68c687fda6ae4.webp)

The electronic throttle control (ETC) is a key component of the engine intake system. Its main function is to adjust the intake air channel area according to the driver's driving intention, thereby controlling the amount of intake air to meet the intake requirements of the engine under different operating conditions. At the same time, the position signal of the throttle valve plate is fed back to the control unit to achieve precise control.

2. Trouble code setting and trouble location:

![](images/4489eed59b1867e80327127081a5718263671736d17913842861f5de191b1a9a.webp)

No Refer to Intermittent trouble check

### 2.2.5.74 Electronic accelerator pedal signal is unreasonable
`geely_coolray_en_cc605ec5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/ff502a82b1ffe55ee74b30618c09af7c62590f31738fdae4005a294844f5b089.webp)

Throttle actuator control system utilizes 2 electronic accelerator pedal position sensors to monitor the position of the electronic accelerator pedal. Electronic accelerator pedal position sensors 1 and 2 are located in pedal assembly. The following circuits are provided in each sensor:

• A 5 V reference voltage circuit • A low level reference voltage circuit • A signal circuit

Use two processors to monitor throttle actuator control system data. Two processors are located in engine control module. Each signal circuit provides signal voltage proportional to pedal movement for two processors. Two processors monitor data of each other to confirm the calculation value of electronic accelerator pedal position displayed is correct.

### 2.2.5.76 Electronic accelerator pedal position sensor 2 signal circuit fault
`geely_coolray_en_141b879b` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/a756cb79ce8f32bad6fbbe74058582d05c568d773dc42ad2b5c4dadf5b60a892.webp)

Throttle actuator control system utilizes 2 electronic accelerator pedal position sensors to monitor the position of the electronic accelerator pedal. Electronic accelerator pedal position sensors 1 and 2 are located in pedal assembly. The following circuits are provided in each sensor:

• A 5 V reference voltage circuit • A low level reference voltage circuit • A signal circuit

Use two processors to monitor throttle actuator control system data. Two processors are located in engine control module. Each signal circuit provides signal voltage proportional to pedal movement for two processors. Two processors monitor data of each other to confirm the calculation value of electronic accelerator pedal position displayed is correct.

### 2.2.5.77 Rear oxygen sensor function fault
`geely_coolray_en_3774d3c0` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/0c8deb673e8db912066c97c5bc779f8165211adba1e4dd173eede8813e3f094b.webp)

The heated rear oxygen sensor (HO2S) is used for fuel control. The sensor compares the oxygen content in the ambient air with the oxygen content in the exhaust stream. Each heated oxygen sensor has a heating element that heats the sensor. The engine control module controls the heating control circuit of the heated oxygen sensor. This allows the system to enter the closed-loop mode earlier, enabling the control module to calculate the air-fuel ratio earlier. The engine control module instructs the heater to be turned on or off to keep the heated oxygen sensor within the specified operating temperature range. The engine control module determines the temperature by measuring the heater current.

2. Trouble code setting and trouble location:

![](images/06e399a611c30481345f7ba9d5ebb091fa58ec70ac357eb432fed07b072e92df.webp)

3. Diagnosis steps:

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_45249fd5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

Before performing these steps, observe the data list of the diagnostic apparatus and analyze the accuracy of each data, which helps to quickly remove the trouble!

A. Connect the scan tool.
B. Start the engine and turn on the scan tool.
C. Keep the engine speed at about 2,500 rpm to warm up for more than two minutes, and measure the oxygen sensor at idle speed so that its working temperature can reach 350℃.
D. Select on the fault diagnostic apparatus: Engine/Read data stream/Rear oxygen sensor voltage.
E. Observe the output voltage of the rear oxygen sensor. The data stream should fluctuate around 0.5V.
F. If the data flow shows that the voltage continues to be below 0.5V (mixed gas is too lean), perform the check steps as follows: • Inject proper amount of propane gas into the air inlet. Observe whether the data stream voltage of the rear oxygen sensor changes significantly, and whether the signal voltage increases rapidly.
G. If the data stream shows that the voltage continues to be higher than 0.5V (mixed gas is too dense), perform the check steps as follows: -Put the transmission gear in Neutral or Park gear. Tighten the hand brake. • Depress the accelerator pedal to suddenly increase the engine speed to 4,000rpm and then quickly release it. Repeat the previous step 3 times or more. • Observe whether the data stream voltage of the rear oxygen sensor changes significantly, and whether the signal voltage decreases rapidly.
H. When performing the above test, the signal voltage of the oxygen sensor should change significantly. Check whether the oxygen sensor model meets the
original requirements.

Replace the rear oxygen sensor. Refer to Replacement of rear oxygen sensor

### 2.2.5.80 Crankshaft-camshaft position correlation malfunction
`geely_coolray_en_1023ea98` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/e98f4d465d8484024b6d8029701202eb6965162eaa5968e7c9bdd2a415d32e39.webp)

The engine control module uses the pulse signals of the crankshaft position sensor and the camshaft position sensor to monitor the correlation between the crankshaft position and the camshaft position. When the crankshaft rotates, it drives the speed sensor signal wheel to rotate together, and the teeth on the signal wheel will cut the magnetic line of the sensor. The change of magnetic flux leads to signal voltage output of a certain frequency at both ends of the sensor coil. The output signal is sent to the engine control module. The output signal represents the speed and position of the crankshaft. The camshaft position sensor is installed at the rear right side of the cylinder head. When the crankshaft rotates, it drives the camshaft and the signal wheel on the camshaft to rotate together through the timing chain. The crankshaft rotates two cycles and the camshaft rotates one cycle correspondingly, and the camshaft position sensor generates voltage to the engine control module under the action of the signal wheel.

2. Trouble code setting and trouble location:

### 2.2.5.82 Front oxygen sensor function fault
`geely_coolray_en_46343119` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Trouble code description:

![](images/5354f0c36eeb1a555b9f95ed564f6bb4e550c7537bf19adc246e8abd2d5daf22.webp)

The heated front oxygen sensor (HO2S) is used for fuel control. The sensor compares the oxygen content in the ambient air with the oxygen content the exhaust stream. Each heated oxygen sensor has a heating element that heats the sensor. The engine control module controls the heating control circuit of the heated oxygen sensor. This allows the system to enter the closed-loop mode earlier, enabling the control module to calculate the air-fuel ratio earlier. The engine control module instructs the heater to be turned on or off to keep the heated oxygen sensor within the specified operating temperature range. The engine control module determines the temperature by measuring the heater current.

2. Trouble code setting and trouble location:

![](images/9148e0f8274a4bce67c760f21457daf21132fe0d005bf6cf2de17c27f3aac9b9.webp)

3. Diagnosis steps:

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_e2ca6c66` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Before performing these steps, observe the data list of the diagnostic apparatus and analyze the accuracy of each data, which helps to quickly remove the trouble!

![](images/84d7679a8881abddca0016c76851b54a8de7f8579ce80a1e16b0e56216d8700e.webp)

A. Connect the scan tool.
B. Start the engine and turn on the scan tool.
C. Keep the engine speed at about 2,500 rpm to warm up for more than two minutes, and measure the oxygen sensor at idle speed so that its working temperature can reach 350℃.
D. Select on the diagnostic apparatus: engine/read data stream/front oxygen sensor voltage.
E. Observe the output voltage of the front oxygen sensor. The data stream should fluctuate within the range of 0.1-0.9V.
F. If the data flow shows that the voltage continues to be below 0.45V (mixed gas is too lean), perform the check steps as follows: • Inject proper amount of propane gas into the air inlet. Observe whether the data flow voltage of the front oxygen sensor changes significantly, and the signal voltage will increase rapidly.
G. If the data stream shows that the voltage continues to be higher than 0.45V (mixed gas is too dense), perform the check steps as follows: • -Put the transmission gear in Neutral or Park gear. Tighten the hand brake. Depress the accelerator pedal to suddenly increase the engine speed to 4,000rpm and then quickly release it. • Repeat the previous step 3 times or more. Observe whether the data flow voltage of the front oxygen sensor changes significantly, and the signal voltage will decrease rapidly.
H. When performing the above test, the signal voltage of the oxygen sensor should change significantly.

Replace the front oxygen sensor. Refer to Replacement of front oxygen sensor

Step 2 Check the air intake system.

A. Use the smoke diffuser to check the air intake system for air leakage. B. Check the intake lines and air filters for blockage. C. Confirm whether the above items are normal.

### 2.2.6.1 Replacement of oil control valve
`geely_coolray_en_498d6ede` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Removal procedure

Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable

2 Remove engine trim cover. Refer to Replacement of engine trim cover

![](images/efd2dd63ac6a9eccd0ff27d3c2669888ddbf0366b5c78191c85a31839572bf1a.webp)

3 Remove the oil control valve a. Disconnect the harness connector A connecting the engine harness and the intake oil control valve. b. Remove the fixing bolt 1 connecting the intake oil control valve and the cylinder head. c. Remove the intake oil control valve.

d. Disconnect the 1 harness connector A connecting the engine harness and the exhaust oil control valve. e. Remove the fixing bolt 1 connecting the exhaust oil control valve and the cylinder head cover. f. Remove the exhaust oil control valve.

![](images/7169be1e75d75e922f53dd298d660b5d6d95f704e728bbed2595d4d28f30f725.webp)

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_2d87f882` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

If the sealing ring of the oil control valve is distorted or damaged, please replace a new oil control valve, and lubricate the O-ring with clean engine oil.

a. Check the oil control valve sealing ring for deformation and damage.

Intake and exhaust VVT components and oil control valve of the same engine must be used in a complete set. Components of different suppliers shall not be installed on the same engine.

![](images/c541ca7279d7f59843af0a16c7f04cd71cf54150ecd35da5325789ac4225c0a3.webp)

b. Install and tighten the fixing bolt 1 connecting the intake oil control valve and the cylinder head.

Torque: 6 N·m

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_5a7c0214` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before installing the intake oil control valve, check whether the appearance of the intake oil control valve is bumpy or whether there are impurities,

Check whether there is foreign matter or impurity in the mounting hole of the intake oil control valve and whether there is sharp flanging in the hole port.

Apply engine oil to the sealing ring of the intake engine oil control valve. After the valve body is loaded coaxially with the hole, no lateral force can be generated during the assembly process.

c. Connect the harness connector A connecting the engine harness and the intake oil control valve.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_8af47fcc` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Firmly plug in harness in the principle of “first plug, second sounds and third confirmations”.

![](images/5ba98aa0e0302b32be91134b0de5c8ab4fd737811f10adf0efda1a1e41895048.webp)

d. Install and tighten the fixing bolt 1 connecting the exhaust oil control valve and the cylinder head cover. Torque: 6 N·m

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_71d8df0c` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before installing the exhaust oil control valve, check whether the appearance of the exhaust oil control valve is bumped or whether there are impurities,

Check whether there is foreign matter or impurity in the mounting hole of the exhaust oil control valve and whether there is sharp flanging in the hole port.

Apply engine oil to the sealing ring of the exhaust oil control valve. The valve body is inserted after it is kept coaxial with the hole, and no lateral force can be generated during the assembly process.

e. Connect the 1 harness connector A connecting the engine harness and the exhaust oil control valve.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_0213a699` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Firmly plug in harness in the principle of “first plug, second sounds and third confirmations”.

2 Install the engine trim cover

3 Connect the negative cable of battery.

### 2.2.6.2 Cleaning of the oil control valve
`geely_coolray_en_c37201cf` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Cleaning procedures

1 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
2 Remove engine trim cover. Refer to Replacement of engine trim cover
3 Remove the oil control valve. Refer to Replacement of Oil Control Valve
4 Clean the oil control valve

a. Use the cleaner to clean the oil inlet hole, oil return hole, oil chambers at angle of entrance and angle of delay oil chambers of the oil control valve.

![](images/f5478a6dbbfdd12dd5e0277bd0d653c3895ce4e85765d802dbf10bf407eb4ed8.webp)

![](images/6731e788fc57ddbb8cdd7a0b9b16c6af1c52a9821a0384f4e8f278647127fd1a.webp)

b. Use an air gun to clean the oil holes and oil chambers of the oil control valve, and clean up the residual cleaner. c. Use 12V voltage to power on and off the oil control valve, let it work in the open and closed statuses, and then clean it with an air gun; repeat 2-3 times.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_73d040c9` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Each power-on time should be shorter than 2s, otherwise the oil control valve may be damaged.

5 Install the oil control valve.
6 Install the engine trim cover
7 Connect the negative cable of battery.

### 2.2.6.3 Replacement of Engine Control Module
`geely_coolray_en_17fce0b2` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Removal procedure

1 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable

2 Remove the left front combination lamp. Refer to Replacement of left combination lamp

3 Remove the engine control module.

![](images/7e95d94b6fdc24adb6912800bed11da170d653b4aff1da5931f2c46a5688468f.webp)

a. Press the harness connector latch, pull up the harness connector handle, and disconnect the 1 harness connector A connecting the front compartment harness assembly with the engine control module.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_c7d3e8ff` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Make sure the handle is completely disengaged and slowly unplug the harness connector horizontally so as not to damage the harness connector and harness pins.

b. Press the harness connector latch, pull up the harness connector handle, and disconnect the harness connector B connecting the engine harness assembly and the engine control module.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_24e703dc` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Make sure the handle is completely disengaged and slowly unplug the harness connector horizontally so as not to damage the harness connector and harness pins.

![](images/9b2d77710166163860435f4fee4e46e2fd7950791dac61718bf1ba6fb3fc78be.webp)

c. Remove the 3 fixing nuts connecting the engine control module and the engine control module bracket.

d. Remove the engine control module.

![](images/baad598b433fc99e43e0f4810744f94ff8b5845f42698f672722bedfdd98d349.webp)

Install the engine control module.

a. Move the engine control module to the installation position.
b. Install and tighten the 3 fixing nuts connecting the engine control module and the engine control module bracket.

Torque: 8 N·m

c. Connect the harness connector B connecting the engine harness assembly and the engine control module, and press down the harness connector handle.

### 2.3.1.2 Fuel system specifications
`geely_coolray_en_7ef720f8` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Fuel injector

![](images/e06d5113536a333e3e01127ebb0d4bb311a9f049925a6648cdd77fcfddf22270.webp)

High-pressure oil rail assembly

Fuel pressure sensor
![](images/fa2e4b9c639a48d43e7bd24af63c963c3df9f3bd73fb49cb2acfe88605bb4f04.webp)

![](images/f917f39b8c164a32fab88f9e732354791bb0bb216058dfeda0f701ccf7d77d4a.webp)

### Fuel tank
`geely_coolray_en_5daec096` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Fuel tank is made of the material such as polystyrene with high density and others. It is fixed by 2 metal hoops connected at the underbody. In addition, it is equipped with fuel steam ventilation valve with roll-over protection function.

### High pressure fuel System
`geely_coolray_en_e851bbd7` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

The fuel system sends the fuel from the fuel tank to the engine. The high-pressure fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor provides high oil pressure for the fuel injector components. The fuel rail delivers the fuel to each injector. Controlled by the electrical signal output by the ECM, the fuel injector injects fuel into the cylinder for combustion according to the predetermined spray mode. The fuel injection quantity is adjusted according to the air pressure in the intake manifold.

### Fuel rail
`geely_coolray_en_db141bf7` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Enough and closed fuel container should be provided to restrain the pulsation of oil pressure of fuel supply system. Ensure that all fuel injectors are provided with sufficient fuel with stable pressure and injected according to the signal input by the ECM.

### Fuel pressure sensor
`geely_coolray_en_afc1fcba` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Fuel pressure sensor is installed at the fuel rail pipe with high pressure. It can directly measure the fuel pressure value of the fuel supply system with high pressure. Through fuel pressure sensor, the closed-loop control of fuel pressure can be achieved. The ECM calculates the theoretically required rail pressure according to the input signal of the relevant sensor under the current engine operating conditions. It can realize the rail pressure control by adjusting the fuel control valve of the high-pressure fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor, and can detect the current actual rail pressure by virtue of the fuel pressure sensor and correct it by comparing it with the theoretical rail pressure to achieve closed-loop control.

### Fuel injector
`geely_coolray_en_da2c53e9` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

It is mainly used to inject fuel into the engine combustion chamber. The timing and duration of fuel injection are controlled by ECM. The engine is equipped with high-pressure fuel injectors designed for direct injection into the cylinder. Fuel is injected into the combustion chamber at a precise injection angle.

### Fuel fuel level sensor assembly
`geely_coolray_en_db26ffd5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The fuel level sensor assembly consists of a fuel level floater and harness arm assembly. Fuel level sensor assembly is integrated in the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor and fuel sensor assembly. The assembly provides variable circuit resistance to the instrument pack according to the contact position of the slider. The circuit harness is led from the varistor and extends to connect with the fuel pump harness connector c/w fuel level sensor.

### 2.3.6.1 Diagnosis description
`geely_coolray_en_c3d4175c` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Be familiar with system functions and operation procedures, and then start system diagnosis. This will help to confirm the correct fault diagnosis steps when a fault occurs. More importantly, it can also help to confirm whether the situation described by the customer belongs to normal operation.

2. The fuel of the vehicle is flammable and explosive. Note that in this process, try not leak fuel. If the fuel leaks, it should be handled in time.

3. Avoid open flames during diagnosis, and be aware that the vehicle shall not have any leakage of electricity.

### 2.3.6.2 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_7ac51a31` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Check after-sales installations that may affect the fuel system, to ensure that these devices cannot affect the fuel system operation.
Check system components that are easily accessible or can be seen to find out if they are obviously damaged or have external leakage.
Check the harness and harness connector to ensure that there is no sign of loosening, damage, poor contact, aging, etc. Check whether the fuel in the fuel tank is the recommended fuel and whether it is sufficient.

### 2.3.6.5 Diagnosis of Surge during Driving
`geely_coolray_en_8bb856dd` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Trouble definition: the engine power changes when the accelerator pedal is stable, causing the vehicle speed to increase and decrease.

Step 7 Connect the fault diagnostic apparatus and check the signal of front oxygen sensor.

a.Connect the scan tool. b.Start the engine and turn on the scan tool. c.Keep the engine speed at about 2,500 rpm to warm up for more than two minutes, and measure the oxygen sensor at idle speed so that its working temperature can reach 350℃. d.Select on the diagnostic apparatus: engine/read data stream/front oxygen sensor voltage. e.Observe the output voltage of the front oxygen sensor. The displayed data stream should fluctuate within the range of 0.1V-0.9 V. If the data stream shows that the voltage continues to be lower than 0.45 V (the gas mixture is too lean), perform the e xamination steps as follows: -Inject proper amount of propane gas into the air inlet. -Observe whether the data stream voltage of the front oxygen sensor changes significantly, and whether the signal voltage increases rapidly. g.If the data stream shows that the voltage continues to be higher than 0.45 V (the gas mixture is too thick), perform the examination steps as follows: -Put the transmission gear in neutral. -Tighten the hand brake. -Depress the accelerator pedal to suddenly increase the engine speed to 4,000rpm and then quickly release the accelerator pedal. -Repeat the previous step 3 times or more. -Observe whether the data stream voltage of the front oxygen sensor changes significantly, and whether the signal voltage decreases rapidly. When performing the above test, the signal voltage of the oxygen sensor should change significantly with the test. Perform corresponding measures according to voltage changes in the table below.

`geely_coolray_en_7efe0916` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Gasoline or gasoline vapor is highly flammable. To avoid the risk of fire or explosion, please keep far away from fire. It is forbidden for operators to use mobile phones when performing these procedures. Do not use open containers to discharge or store gasoline. Please prepare a dry chemical fire extinguisher nearby before performing these procedures.

Wrap a rag around the fuel pressure gauge and the fuel rail joint, enabling to absorb the leaked fuel when connecting the fuel pressure gauge, and reducing the risk of fire and injury. When the test is complete, place the rag in the designated container. Clean the oil pipe connector before removing the oil pipe.

Warning！

It is forbidden to discharge fuel into open containers, or store fuel in open containers, otherwise a fire may be caused.

### 2.3.7.1 Fuel pressure release procedures
`geely_coolray_en_ac9454fc` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

![](images/417e92d27f1bdd32083a07efdbecfeafa6775e8f9dac07102093e640b638bb96.webp)

1 Open the engine trim cover and pull out the fuse EF06 (20A) of fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor from the engine compartment.
2 Start the engine until the engine stalls automatically.
3 Restart the engine after the engine stalls and allow the crankshaft to continue rotating for about 10s.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_283be045` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

If you want to remove any fuel system components, wrap up the line joints with plastic bags to prevent fuel leakage and foreign objects from entering.

### Warning！
`geely_coolray_en_ab2b161e` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Prohibit discharging or storing fuel in the open container. Be sure to use the approved fuel storage container to reduce the possibility of fire and explosion.

### Warning！
`geely_coolray_en_e9959d53` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Prepare a dry chemical (Class B) fire extinguisher nearby before performing on-board maintenance procedures. If these cautions are not followed, it may result in personal injury.

![](images/c06dc5a95010947f5ef30a3fdf56eaa2599f8e5d13f50e9daa617bf5a433dbeb.webp)

1 Remove fuel filler cap.
2 Open the fuel filler cap.
3 Insert the hose into the fuel tank until the hose touches the bottom of the fuel tank.

`geely_coolray_en_6bf65628` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Removal procedure Open the engine compartment cover 2 Release fuel system pressure, refer to Fuel pressure release procedures

3 Disconnect the negative cable of battery, refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable Lift the vehicle, please refer to Lifting and jacking of vehicle
5 Remove the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly a. Remove the grounding wire bolt of the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly.

![](images/cc058b29f422359b9db79fab19bb02be56685ba8da8b46b09fd114839e5c47b3.webp)

![](images/875e5831b48ddedea810d6349c6830087d8bd0fec247b801b1bfc6d92f8394f3.webp)

b. Disconnect the fuel pipeline 1 at both ends of the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_09c88c6a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

If it is difficult to remove silt after it has entered the oil pipe joint, gently knock the filter housing with the wooden handle to make the silt and sand vibrate. First, squeeze and hold the lock plate of the quickplug connector, and then pull out the quick-plug connector from the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly.

c. Remove the fixing bolt 2 on the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly bracket, and remove the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly.

1 Install the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly a. Install the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly on the bracket, and tighten the fixing bolt 2 of the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly. Torque: 3 N m b. Connect pipeline 1 at both ends of the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly.

![](images/bc7e03726991c98bb5381c8cbf66dd832cc36a4c4f1207cf3b33601aff9137f1.webp)

c. Connect the grounding wire of the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly, and tighten the fixing bolts. Torque: 10 N m

### 2.3.7.4 Replacement of fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor (Type I)
`geely_coolray_en_ec495ef8` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Removal procedure

1 Open the engine compartment cover.
2 Release the pressure in the fuel system. Refer to Procedures for fuel pressure release
3 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
4 Remove the rear seat cushion. Refer to Replacement of Rear Seat Cushion
5 Remove the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor a. Remove the fuel tank access cover. b. Disconnect the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor harness connector 1.
c. Disconnect the oil outlet pipe 2 of the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor.
d. Disconnect the fuel return hose 3 of the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor. e. Use a special tool to remove the fuel tank cap in the direction of the arrow.
Special tool: 4114720075 f. Take out from the fuel tank the fuel pump assembly c/w fuel level sensor and fuel sensor.
g. Take out the sealing ring 2 of the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor.

![](images/49804b36cb325eedc9214433c83d297e4773ee484634f69e881001978d4f0fc4.webp)

![](images/eec173c01cfe577c9a9fba792d795b4d956000c255e51941c02ff177c1e89a1e.webp)

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_f4ae7620` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:body | p:1

Take out vertically to prevent the fuel level sensor from being damaged. During the disassembly, notice that fuel should not drip on the floor and body interior trims, otherwise it will corrode the floor sealant and body interior trims.

Installation procedure

![](images/2470dbd9f9b457cb0f7e92259946434f33ffaef41d551e88f37ef7baa6d0a8fe.webp)

1 Install the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor a. Clean the joint surface between the sealing ring of the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor and the fuel tank, and install a new sealing ring 2 of the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor. b. Install the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor in place.

c. Use a special tool to lock the fuel tank cover in the direction of the arrow.
Special tool: 4114720075

d. Connect the fuel outlet pipe 2 of the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor and fuel sensor assembly. e. Connect the fuel return pipe 3 of the fuel pump assembly c/w fuel level sensor and fuel sensor. f. Connect the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor and fuel sensor assembly harness connector 1.

![](images/c25a2b4dc644182d71ec9e172ef7e088d3af9d7d2415008638bca1b287043aa8.webp)

g. Install the fuel tank access cover plate.

2 Install the rear seat cushion.
3 Connect the negative cable of battery.
4 Close the engine compartment cover.

### 2.3.7.6 Replacement of fuel tank assembly (Type I)
`geely_coolray_en_81ae3d32` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Removal procedure

1 Open the engine compartment cover.
2 Release the pressure in the fuel system. Refer to Procedures for fuel pressure release
3 Drain the fuel tank. Refer to Fuel tank draining procedure
4 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
5 Remove the rear seat cushion. Refer to Replacement of Rear Seat Cushion
6 Lift the vehicle. Refer to Lifting and Jacking of Vehicle Remove the middle muffler assembly. Refer to Replacement of middle muffler assembly for replacement

8 Replacement of fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly to be removed. Refer to Replacement of fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly

9 Remove the fuel tank assembly a. Remove the fuel tank access cover.

![](images/b99806a1d9046b5ae9b06b492cd73d30d317d91073e8e9e9e1476487e224ec1f.webp)

![](images/80669984f071b2636b2d9f2abb0db4f20442553e2c94c51a484f9a23afd25eea.webp)

b. Disconnect the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor harness connector 1.
c. Disconnect the fuel inlet pipe 2 and fuel return pipe 3 of the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor. d. Loosen the clamp and remove the fuel tank filler pipe 1.
e. Fuel tank ventilation hose 2.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_89bdfddc` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:body | p:1

Block the fuel pipe with a rag to prevent polluting the fuel tank; loosen the ventilation hose of the fuel tank.

![](images/4c36aa03117bd320447c297e04cad91be563be7a324e0fb657b6d050449870eb.webp)

f. Disconnect the OBD sensor harness connector 1. g. Disconnect the connection between the fuel tank ventilation pipe 2 and the canister. h. Disconnect the canister outlet pipe 3 from the canister.

i. Disconnect the lower floor oil supply pipe 1 from the oil outlet pipe of the filter. j. Disconnect the connection between lower floor ventilation pipe 2 and the canister outlet pipe.

k. Use a hydraulic lifter to support the fuel tank assembly. l. Remove the 4 fixing bolts connecting the fuel tank assembly and the vehicle body. m. Slowly lower the fuel tank assembly by hydraulic lifter, disconnect the connected pipeline of the fuel tank assembly, and separate the fuel tank assembly.

![](images/8957a5ddd5c51db3a37a65fbdba975c6a6f17dd8598412597701831d24282ccf.webp)

Install the fuel tank assembly

a. Fasten the fuel pipeline on the fuel tank and use a hydraulic lifter to lift the fuel tank to the installation
position.
b. Install and tighten the 4 fixing bolts connecting the fuel tank bracket and the vehicle body.
Torque: 45 N m (metric system) c. Connect the lower floor oil supply pipe 1 with the oil outlet pipe of the filter.
d. Connect the lower floor ventilation pipe 2 with the canister outlet pipe. e. Connect the OBD sensor harness connector 1.
f. Connect the fuel tank ventilation pipe 2 with the canister.
g. Connect the canister air outlet pipe 3 with the canister. h. Install the fuel filler pipe of the fuel tank in place and tighten the clamp 1.
i. Fuel tank ventilation hose 2.

![](images/5b99b3199fe5903c9dbb6cb61129e20ff1884c71199ae9391076085d927420af.webp)

j. Connect the fuel outlet pipe 2 and the fuel return hose 3 of the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor c/w fuel sensor assembly. k. Connect the fuel pump c/w fuel level sensor and fuel sensor assembly harness connector 1.

l. Install the fuel tank access cover plate.

2 Install the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly.
3 Install the middle muffler assembly.
4 Lower the vehicle.
5 Install the rear seat cushion.
6 Connect the negative cable of battery.
7 Close the engine compartment cover.

Disconnect the quick connector B connecting the lower floor ventilation pipe and the fuel tank assembly.

This step requires cooperation of two persons.
b. Install and tighten the 4 fixing bolts connecting the fuel tank assembly and the vehicle body.

c. Clamp the fuel tank assembly pipe to the double-pipe clamp C. d. Connect the quick connector B connecting th e canister air intake pipe and the canister. e. Connect the quick connector A connecting the canister outlet pipe and the canister.

f. Connect the 1 quick connector B connecting the lower floor ventilation pipe and the fuel tank assembly. g. Connect the quick connector A connecting the lower floor oil supply pipe and the fuel tank assembly. h. Install and tighten the fixing bolt 1 connecting the fuel filter c/w grounding wire assembly and the vehicle body. Torque: 10 N·m

![](images/be759837eb5dcc6f626e1340589ac0b76d64cd463e6f8f5cf9b241487563e79a.webp)

i. Move the fuel filler pipe to the installation position and install the 2 fixing clamps connecting the fuel tank filler pipe assembly with the fuel tank assembly.

j. Connect the 中 harness connector connecting the floor harness to the fuel tank assembly.

`geely_coolray_en_bf77f1d4` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

`geely_coolray_en_b4b08dd8` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

### 2.3.7.10 Replacement of fuel-rail and fuel injector subassembly
`geely_coolray_en_a2295ad2` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Removal procedure

1 Release the pressure in the fuel system. Refer to Procedures for fuel pressure release
2 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
3 Remove engine trim cover. Refer to Replacement of engine trim cover
4 Remove the high-pressure oil pipe components. Refer to Replacement of high-pressure oil pipe components
5 Dismount the ignition coil. Refer to Replacement of Ignition Coil

![](images/239ea61766d5f0dcc99dd65258c245aa008285380bd5e6763085544d4d71a9eb.webp)

6 Remove the fuel injector subassembly of fuel rail.

a. Disconnect the 1 harness connector A connecting the engine harness and the fuel injector sub-assembly of fuel rail. b. Remove the 4 fixing bolts 1 connecting the fuel injector sub-assembly of fuel rail and the cylinder head. c. Remove the fuel injector sub-assembly of fuel rail.

d. When the fuel injector cannot be removed as a whole with the fuel rail assembly, use a special tool to pull out the fuel injector.

Special tools for removing fuel injectors: 4114870402
Special tool for pulling hammer:4114870403

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_3444c1b5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Install the fuel injector on the fuel rail components correctly, place the fuel injector sub-assembly of the fuel rail in a suitable container, and then cover it with non-woven fabrics to prevent dust from entering.

#品 TT7T

![](images/701a674adc4fda81538aeecb4ea440ce2c9d6bcbc49409e507427b2dad97db64.webp)

1 Install the fuel injector sub-assembly of fuel rail.

a. Check whether the sealing ring of fuel injector on the fuel injector sub-assembly of fuel rail is deformed, damaged, and whether the installation is in place.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_176cc793` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

If the Teflon sealing ring of the fuel injector is distorted or damaged, please replace a new fuel injector.

Lubrication oil is not allowed to be applied on the Teflon sealing ring of the fuel injector.

b. Align the fuel injector on the fuel rail and fuel injector sub-assembly with the mounting holes, and press it at a uniform speed along the common axis of the fuel injector. c. Fasten the 4 fixing bolts 1 connecting the fuel injector sub-assembly of fuel rail and the cylinder head multiple times in accordance with the order of cylinders 2-4-1-3 (each bolt shall be screwed in 2-3 turns and replaced by other bolts).

Torque: 25 N·m

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_b86654ee` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

When moving the fuel injector sub-assembly of fuel rail, it is not allowed to hold the fuel injector or fuel pressure sensor by hand.

Do not touch part pins.

During the power-on operation such as cold and hot testing, it is not allowed to plug and pull out parts connectors with power on.

Prevent parts from falling or being impacted, and fallen parts must be scrapped.

d. Connect the harness connector A connecting the engine harness and the fuel injector sub-assembly of fuel rail.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_7e2cb2fd` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Firmly plug in harness in the principle of “first plug, second sounds and third confirmations”

2 Mount the ignition coil.

3 Install the high-pressure oil pipe components.
4 Install the engine trim cover
5 Connect the negative cable of battery.

### 2.3.7.11 Replacement of lower floor oil supply pipe
`geely_coolray_en_5fced599` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Removal procedure

1 Remove engine trim cover. Refer to Replacement of engine trim cover
2 Release the pressure in the fuel system. Refer to Procedures for fuel pressure release
3 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
4 Remove the air filter corrugated pipe. Refer to Replacement of air filter corrugated pipe
5 Lift the vehicle. Refer to Lifting and Jacking of Vehicle
6 Remove the left bottom shield. Refer to Replacement of left bottom shield

### 2.4.3.1 Instructions and Operations
`geely_coolray_en_fde8980a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

The basic principle adopted by the evaporative emission control system is the carbon canister storage method. This method transfers fuel vapor from the fuel tank to the activated carbon storage device so as to preserve the vapor when the vehicle is not running. When the engine is running, fuel vapor is sucked from the carbon core by the intake air flow and consumed during normal combustion. Gasoline vapor flows from the fuel tank into the fuel line marked with fuel vapor recovery. This vapor is absorbed by the canister. When the engine runs for a specified period of time, the engine control module provides a grounding circuit to energize the EVAP canister cleanup spurge solenoid, and air is drawn into the canister and mixed with the vapor. Then, this mixture is sucked into the intake manifold. The opening and closing of the EVAP canister clean-up solenoid is controlled by the pulse width modulation (PWM) signal. According to the operating conditions determined by air flow, fuel regulation and intake air temperature, the duty cycle of the pulse width modulation of the EVAP canister clean-up spurge solenoid changes.

The EVAP system is a component of the fuel system and is used to prevent fuel vapor from being exhausted into the surrounding air. Fuel vapor spilled from the fuel tank must not be discharged into the atmosphere. It must be sent to the intake manifold through the canister. Fuel vapor will burn in the engine.

Fuel vapor in the fuel tank is led to the canister from the turnover (accident) relief valve on the top of the fuel tank through a hose. The turnover (accidental) relief valve can prevent fuel leakage, and when a turnover accident occurs, the valve is closed. The canister is an activated carbon storage device, which can purify fuel vapor. After purification, fuel vapor is distributed to the intake manifold through the fuel pipe and enters the engine cylinder for combustion. Install the intake manifold on the fuel pipe. The canister solenoid valve should be installed. The canister solenoid valve controls the fuel vapor that is introduced into the engine. The control valve opens and closes the connection between the canister and intake manifold. The flow rate of the canister solenoid valve is controlled by ECM. The canister has an air inlet. When fuel vapor is released into the intake manifold, underpressure will occur in the canister, and the air inlet can compensate for the insufficient pressure. The canister air inlet includes an air filter. The following conditions can lead to poor idling, speed loss and poor maneuverability:

The hose is disconnected, cracked, and not properly connected to the correct pipe.

The canister solenoid valve does not work.
The canister is damaged.

The EVAP canister is an emission control device containing activated carbon particles. The EVAP canister is used to store fuel vapor from the fuel tank. When certain conditions are met, the engine control module will energize the canister solenoid valve, causing fuel vapor to be drawn into the engine cylinder and burned.

### 2.4.4.1 Operating Principles of the canister solenoid valve
`geely_coolray_en_2744cec6` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Canister solenoid valve is composed of solenoid coil, strainer, armature and valve.

The airflow rate of the canister solenoid valve is related to the following conditions:

ECM controls the duty cycle of electric pulse of canister solenoid valve according to the signals provided by the sensors of the engine.

—The pressure difference between the inlet and outlet of the canister solenoid valve.

When there is no electrical pulse received by the canister solenoid valve, the canister solenoid valve is closed. ECM only controls the operation of the canister solenoid valve when a series of factors such as water temperature, engine state, load, etc. meet the setting requirements, but the canister solenoid valve does not operate under the following conditions:

A period of time after the engine cold starts.

Engine coolant temperature is relatively low. The engine is in the idle operation phase.
—The engine is in the large load phase.
— There is a fault of an important sensor of the system.

### 2.4.6.1 Diagnosis description
`geely_coolray_en_f564f8c7` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before diagnosing the faults of the auxiliary emission control devices, refer to Instructions and Operations and System Operating Principle. Understand and be familiar with the working principle of the auxiliary emission control device, and then start system agnosis. This will help to confirm the correct fault diagnosis steps when a fault occurs. More importantly, it can also help to confirm whether the situation described by the customer belongs to normal operation. Any fault diagnosis of the auxiliary emission control device should start with a routine inspection that guides the serviceman to take the next logical step for troubleshooting. Understanding and using the diagnosis flow chart correctly can shorten the time of diagnosis and avoid misjudgment of the faulty part.

Precautions for maintenance of canister solenoid valve:

1. During installation, the airflow direction must comply with the regulations.
2. When it is found that black particles inside the valve body of the canister solenoid valve cause the control valve to fail and that the canister solenoid valve needs to be replaced, check the canister.
3. Avoid liquids such as water and oil from entering the valve during maintenance.
4. In order to avoid the transmission of solid sound, it is recommended to install the canister control valve in the air above the hose.

### 2.4.6.2 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_bb0ae138` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

Check after-sale fittings to ensure that they do not affect performance of the motor control system.

Check system components that are easily accessible or can be seen to find out if there is any obvious damage of the component or there is a situation that may cause a fault.

Check whether the fuel in the fuel tank is the recommended fuel and whether it is sufficient.

### 2.4.6.4 Positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) System Check and Diagnosis
`geely_coolray_en_9c095f39` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Consequences of incorrect operation

1. The crankcase ventilation channel of small load is blocked and the crankcase ventilation rubber hose of heavy load is blocked, which will lead to the following faults:

Idle fluctuation. - High engine oil consumption

2. The leakage of heavy load hose of crankcase ventilation may cause the following faults:
- Idle fluctuatio n. Incompliance with regulatory requirements.

3. The leakage of the large load check valve of crankcase ventilation towards the interior engine causes the following faults:

Idle fluctuation. - High engine oil consumption

4. The failure of check valve in the air supply channel of crankcase ventilation causes the following faults: - High engine oil consumption

5. The failure of the small load check valve of crankcase ventilation causes the following faults:
- High engine oil consumption

### 2.5.2.1 Instructions and Operations
`geely_coolray_en_411d6c45` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Cylinder head

The main function of the cylinder head is to seal the cylinder. The cylinder head and the piston form a combustion space, which is affected by high-temperature and high-pressure gas. The cylinder head bears the mechanical load caused by gas forces and tightened cylinder bolts. At the same time, it also bears high heat load caused by contact with high-temperature gas. In order to ensure the good sealing of the cylinder, the cylinder head must not be damaged or deformed. Therefore, the cylinder head should have sufficient strength and rigidity.

### Camshaft
`geely_coolray_en_5f88e027` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

The camshaft rotates continuously and drives the hydraulic valve rod to move up and down. Then, it controls the opening and closing of intake and exhaust valves.

Double overhead camshafts are adopted, that is, there are two camshafts. One camshaft controls the intake valve, and the other camshaft controls the exhaust valve. Camshafts are located on the top of the engine. The bearing block of the cylinder head is fixed by the camshaft cover. The borehole on the camshaft journal of the cylinder head is used as an oil passage. Under the influence of pressure, engine oil flows down to the camshaft and lubricates each camshaft journal. Engine oil flows back to the oil pan through the oil return hole on the cylinder head. The cam lobe is machined. And at the right time, the intake and exhaust valves are accurately opened and closed by adding the right amount. Camshaft lobe can be lubricated through the splash effect of the high-pressure engine oil that escapes from the camshaft journal.

Timing chain assembly

The timing chain assembly is mainly used to rotate the crankshaft and camshaft (intake camshaft and exhaust camshaft) synchronously to open and close the intake and exhaust valves at the appropriate time for the intake and exhaust strokes of each cylinder. The inner surface of the timing chain assembly has teeth and are driven by the crankshaft.

Piston

The function of the piston is to bear the air pressure and transmit it to the connecting rod through the piston pin, pushing the crankshaft to rotate. The top of the piston is also part of the combustion chamber.

Timing gear chain tensioner

The timing chain tensioner is mainly used to adjust the tension of the timing chain assembly to prevent the timing chain assembly from disconnecting.

Crankshaft

The crankshaft is the most important component of the engine. It absorbs the force transmitted by the connecting rod, converts it into torque, and outputs and drives other accessories on the engine through the crankshaft. The crankshaft is affected by the combined action of the centrifugal force of rotating weight, the periodic changing inertia force and the reciprocating inertia force. Thus, the crankshaft bearing is subject to bending and twisting load.

Crankshaft timing sprocket wheel

The main function of the crankshaft timing sprocket wheel is to transfer power from the crankshaft to the camshaft through the timing chain assembly.

### 2.5.3.1 Working principle of reciprocating piston engine
`geely_coolray_en_0dd3fa42` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Intake stroke

The exhaust valve is closed and the intake valve is opened. The piston is driven by the crankshaft from top dead center to bottom dead center. During the movement of the piston, the cylinder volume gradually increases, and a certain vacuum degree is formed in the cylinder. ECM controls the fuel injector assembly to inject fuel into the cylinder, the intake valve opens, and air is drawn into the cylinder through the intake passage, thereby forming a combustible gas mixture.

Compression stroke

Intake and exhaust valves are closed. After the air inlet stroke completes, the piston is driven by the crankshaft from bottom dead center to top dead center. As the piston moves, the volume of the cylinder decreases, which compresses the combustible mixture and causes its temperature to rise rapidly.

Power stroke

Intake and exhaust valves remain closed. At the end of the compression stroke, ECM controls the primary coil loop of the ignition coil to be disconnected, and a high voltage is induced at the secondary coil. The high voltage is quickly transmitted to the spark plug installed at the top of the cylinder head through the ignition wire, and finally breaks through the spark plug gap to generate an electric spark, igniting the combustible gas mixture in the cylinder. The flame is quickly transmitted to the entire combustion chamber, and the gas mixture in the cylinder gives off a large amount of heat energy with the volume expanding rapidly and pressure and temperature rising at the same time. The pressure of expansion acts on the top of the piston, causing it to move from top dead center to bottom dead center. Reciprocating motion of the piston is converted into the rotational motion by the connecting rod.

### Exhaust stroke
`geely_coolray_en_bac5054b` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Exhaust valve is opened and intake valve remains closed. Under the action of the connecting rod, the crankshaft drives the piston from the bottom dead center to the top dead center. The inflated combustible gas is exhausted out the cylinder driven by residual pressure and the piston. When the piston reaches the top dead center, the exhaust stroke is completed and the exhaust valve is closed.

But in the actual design, the inlet valve opens earlier than the top dead center and closes later than the bottom dead center. It aims at making the inlet of air more full and reducing the energy loss in the inlet process. The exhaust valve will be activated before the bottom dead center and be closed later than the top dead center. It aims at reducing combustible residual gases in the cylinder and reducing the energy loss in the inlet process. The design will allow the exhaust valve to have a certain overlap angle, that is, exhaust valves are open in a certain crankshaft angle. At this time, the combustible residual gas is discharged through the exhaust valve, which has certain inertia and makes the inlet of air more full to some extent. While it is not that the larger the valve overlap angle, the better. Engines under different operating conditions have different requirements for valve overlap, hence the variable valve timing system used in the engine, aiming at meeting different needs of engines for overlap angles under different operating conditions.

### 2.5.3.2 Working principle of VVT system
`geely_coolray_en_5b4d1a13` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Working principle of VVT system

VVT is short for Variable Valve Timing, which refers to the variable timing valve system. Everything that has mass has inertia, and because of inertia, the air that is drawn into the engine cylinder also retains the tendency to enter the cylinder after the intake process ends. The engine speed has an influence on the intake and exhaust flows and the combustion process in the cylinder. When the engine runs at high speed, the intake air flows at a high rate with much inertial energy, so it is desirable that the intake valve opens earlier and closes later and draws as much mixed gas as possible in the cylinder; conversely, when the engine runs at low speed, the intake air flows at a low rate with little inertia energy. If the intake valve opens prematurely, because the piston is exhausting upward at this time, it is easy to expel fresh gas from the cylinder, decreasing the amount of the intake air, and the engine works more unstably. Therefore, during low-speed operation, it is desirable that the engine intake valve be opened slightly later. In order to achieve balance, in general profile design of cam, the valve timing must take account of conditions at both high speed and low speed, so it is a compromise gas distribution scheme.

VVT control strategy
![](images/cb3825942aec8512270bd2ff026aa067fe63df173a8088eabb0ec750de1ed433.webp)

![](images/e4fbb346108fc6fa10c5e75de73d795ef77ae140d8344fbb31912d4d634d7769.webp)

The advancing process

When the engine is running normally, the oil pressure generated by the oil pump acts on the central oil control valve. ECM uses pulse width modulation signal to control the central oil control valve. When ECM needs to adjust the intake valve to the maximum advance position, it controls the central oil control valve opening as 100%. At this time, the pressure in the advance chamber is greater than the pressure in the lag chamber, and VVT rotor blades generate a phase angle that is ahead of crankshaft angle, and finally stays at the maximum advance position. At this time, the VVT phase advances.

The lagging process

When the engine is running normally, the oil pressure generated by the oil pump acts on the central oil control valve. ECM uses pulse width modulation signal for the central oil control valve. If ECM expects the current VVT adjustment of the intake valve to be in the maximum lag position, the opening degree of the central oil control valve controlled by ECM is 0%, and oil pressure enters the lag chamber of the VVT actuator. Therefore, VVT rotor blade produces displacement in the same direction relative to crankshaft angle, and finally stays at the maximum position.

### 2.5.6.2 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_c79d16d5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Check after-sales installations that may affect the performance of the mechanical system.

Check system components that are easily accessible or can be seen to find out if there is any obvious damage or there is a situation that may cause a malfunction.
Confirm whether the engine lubrication oil level is normal and whether the oil viscosity is normal.
• Record specific factors such as engine speed and ambient temperature.
Compare with a known good engine to confirm whether the current engine condition is normal.

### 2.5.6.4 Engine noise diagnosis
`geely_coolray_en_ad7cbf22` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Engine vibration actually refers to the resonance noise of the engine. When the vibration frequency of the engine and the vibration frequency of the point of trouble are the same, the noise will be perceived. n the case severe vibration, the noise is usually loud and is caused by broken or severely worn internal parts of the engine. In the case of slight vibration, noise can be heard but not loud. The reason for the slight vibration is the wear of the internal parts of the engine, and the loose or broken external parts of the engine can also cause severe or slight vibration. When diagnosing noise faults, the source of resonant excitation must be found to troubleshoot.

Diagnostic hints: The symptom may be an intermittent trouble caused by dampness of the drive belt or pulley. It may be necessary to spray a small amount of water on the drive belt to reproduce the trouble reported by the customer. If the symptom reappears after spraying water, clean the pulley. Loose or improper installation of body parts, suspension parts or other vehicle parts may also cause chirp.

Trouble definition: The following conditions are symptoms of chirp of drive belt

You can hear a chirp noise every time you turn the drive belt.
– Noise usually appears on rainy days or cold mornings.

Trouble definition: The following conditions are symptoms of squeal of drive belt

Squeal caused by slipping drive belts.

Noise occurs when a large load is applied to the drive belt, such as the startup of the compressor of the A/C system, the rapid opening of the throttle valve when the engine is running, or the squeal caused by the drive belt slipping on the faulty accessory drive part.

### 2.5.6.12 Diagnosis of Drive Belt Falling off
`geely_coolray_en_341831b4` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Diagnostic hints: If the drive belt repeatedly falls off from the drive pulley, the cause is the misalignment of the pulley. If the accessory drive component causes the load of the transmission belt to increase or decrease, the drive belt may be detached from the pulley. Check whether the accessory drive component works normally. If the drive belt is of improper length, the tensioner will not be able to maintain the proper tension of the drive belt.

Fault definition: The drive belt gets adrift from the belt pulley or the drive belt cannot be correctly installed on the belt pulley

Step 1 Check the drive belt for damage, and replace with a new drive belt if necessary.

Next step

Step 5 Check whether the drive belt tensioner works normally, and repair the faulty part.

Next step

### 2.5.6.13 Diagnosis of Excessive Wear of Drive Belt
`geely_coolray_en_a79d1f7a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Diagnostic hints: Excessive wear of the drive belt is usually caused by improper installation or using the wrong drive belt. A slight misalignment of the drive pulley will not cause excessive wear, but it is likely to cause the drive belt to make noise or fall off. Severe misalignment of the drive belt pulley can cause excessive wear and also cause the drive belt to fall off.

Fault definition: Wear of the outer edge of the drive belt due to improper installation of the drive belt.

5 Remove the belt tensioner. a. Remove the 3 fixing bolts connecting the belt tensioner and the alternator. b. Remove the tensioner mechanism components.

![](images/fc9494364b9f52a3cf44b9141d32b58807077add1bf6dd97922cdeab113ff2c6.webp)

![](images/9e19c8c201c1289b526b81d15e309c492c2680a94da160f2a2cd813c6a94214d.webp)

### Installation procedure
`geely_coolray_en_b6fb05b3` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1 Install the belt tensioner. a. Move the belt tensioner to the installation position. b. Pre-tighten the 3 hexagon flange bolts by 2-3 teeth, and then use appropriate torque wrench to tighten the bolts respectively. Torque: 24 N·m

2 Install the drive belt.
3 Install the engine bottom shield.
4 Install the right front wheel.
5 Lower the vehicle.
