### 2.5.7.9 Replacement of front oil seal of crankshaft
`geely_coolray_en_6581152f` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Removal procedure

1 Lift the vehicle. Refer to Lifting and Jacking of Vehicle 2 Remove the bottom shield of the engine. Refer to Replacement of engine bottom shield

3 Remove the damping pulley. Refer to Replacement of drive belt
4 Use special tools to remove the crankshaft front oil seal. Special tool: 4114870386

![](images/b8ec3b0f2747f87c13c66a31104788a20a8b3e23b6bfcce2e172866658c4b05b.webp)

Installation procedure

![](images/717412caac107f09fb4c2d501643fdcd4d15a127180ac5215fa38760d36532e3.webp)

Use special tools to install the crankshaft front oil seal. Special tool: 4114870595

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_f308cea0` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

1. The front oil seal of the crankshaft shall not be reused, and must be replaced with a new one after each removal. 2. Check the oil seal lips for foreign matters. During installation, there should be no foreign objects on the lip. 3. Before pressing and installing the crankshaft front oil seal, evenly apply engine oil to the timing cover oil seal mounting hole for lubrication. 4. The outer surface of the crankcase oil seal must not have obvious oil stains accumulation. 5. The distance between the end face of the front oil seal of the pressed crankshaft and the end face of the mounting hole is 0.5 mm-1 mm. 6. Measure the step difference between the end face of the front oil seal and the end face of the oil seal of timing cover cover, which shall be ≤ 0.4 mm.
2 Install the damping belt pulley.
3 Install the engine bottom shield. Lower the vehicle.

`geely_coolray_en_a6c4434b` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Torque: 10 N·m

i. Connect the quick connector A connecting the radiator assembly ventilation pipe and the expansion tank water outlet pipe.

hose and the intake manifold.

r. Install and tighten the 2 fixing bolts 1 connecting the engine harness and the cylinder head cover subassembly.

Torque: N·m

a. Connect the 1 harness connector A connecting the engine harness and the high-pressure oil pump.

t. Install the 3 harness clips connecting the engine harness with the cylinder head cover subassembly.

### 2.5.7.12 Replacement of timing chain tensioner repair kit
`geely_coolray_en_21532d83` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Removal procedure

1 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
2 Remove the supercharger intake muffler. Refer to Replacement of supercharger intake muffle
3 Lift the vehicle. Refer to Lifting and Jacking of Vehicle
4 Remove the engine bottom shield. Refer to Replacement of engine bottom shield
5 Remove the timing chain tensioner

![](images/c095986249f45274e25c3cc0d1e5f25a7cd62bad8668f5dd726c33103381c42d.webp)

![](images/68701273f945859aab5db34dcb037bf4502f30659d4ef942753974d4d0ba86bb.webp)

a. Remove the 2 fixing nuts connecting the timing chain tensioner and the cylinder block. b. Remove the timing chain tensioner.

c. Remove the timing chain tensioner gasket.

d. Remove the clamp of the timing chain tensioner from the first ring and place it at the second ring position 2.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_35768119` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:1

When clamp 1 is installed to the second ring, the clamp notch is aligned with the timing chain tensioner housing notch.

If the timing chain tensioner is disassembled during removal, it shall be directly scrapped.

e. Install the latch 3.

f. Press the timing chain tensioner and press the clamp 1 back into the first ring.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_509f92fa` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

During the pressing process, it is necessary to continuously move the clamp 4 in the direction of the arrow.

Installation procedure

1 Install the timing chain tensioner

![](images/c48ed385871834dd77c640b7ad41de223c2fea0de4fc35cfe935ff4f0efcadd1.webp)

a. Move the timing chain tensioner gasket to the installation position.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_0ac24ffc` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The gasket of the timing chain tensioner is a disposable part and shall be replaced after removal.

Pay attention to the assembly as per the requirements in the figure. After the assembly, the side of the anti-error mark shall be as shown in the figure.

b. Unplug the upper latch of the timing chain tensioner.

![](images/5d67924cee3b17438116408e4e8a8402b14e7124157ef39de7954e3395bf0c53.webp)

c. Move the timing chain tensioner to the installation position.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_d0a30c2f` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

When installing the timing chain tensioner, apply oil evenly to the contact between the timing chain tensioner journal and the oil seal lip.

d. Install and tighten the 2 fixing nuts connecting the timing chain tensioner and the cylinder block.

Torque: 10 N·m

e. Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise for 90° to ensure that the tensioner pops up, and then turn the crankshaft clockwise to return to its original position.

2 Install the lower shield assembly of engine.
3 Lower the vehicle.
4 Install the supercharger intake muffler.
5 Connect the negative cable of battery.

### 2.5.7.13 Replacement of timing cover repair kit emoval procedure
`geely_coolray_en_37f48ee1` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

1 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
2 Remove the right vibration insulator. Refer to Replacement of Right Vibration Insulator
3 Lift the vehicle. Refer to Lifting and Jacking of Vehicle Remove the bottom shield of the engine. Refer to Replacement of engine bottom shield
5 Remove the timing chain tensioner Refer to Replacement of timing chain tensioner
6 Remove the belt tensioner. Refer to Replacement of belt tensioner
7 Remove the crankshaft front oil seal. Refer to Replacement of crankshaft front oil seal
8 Remove the cylinder head cover subassembly. Refer to Replacement of cylinder head cover subassembly
9 Remove the supercharger intake muffler. Refer to Replacement of supercharger intake muffler

10 Remove the timing cover a. Disconnect the harness connector A connecting the engine harness and the electronic oil pump. b. Disconnect the 3 harness clips B connecting the engine harness and the timing cover and move away the harness.

![](images/a8f7dbebbf61ca4073e1376caf70e804043287b9b98b8c64585940ea51882aba.webp)

### 1 Install the timing cover
`geely_coolray_en_7344b4eb` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

![](images/bb12edc9894ffebf134b439b85f01dd653b3f2560f10fb80c62ac37f08bd61a5.webp)

a. Spray modified alcohol or similar medium on the clean white cloth, wipe the timing cover joint surface, wait for the modified alcohol or similar medium to evaporate, and then spray Loctite 1455 on the clean white cloth and wipe the timing cover joint surface. The white cloth used for two wipes should not be mixed for use.

b. Test with a 32# Dane pen. After passing, apply Loctite 5900 sealant on the timing cover, and the track of the glue line and the diameter of the glue line shall be subject to the requirements in the figure.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_0bcce0e7` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The diameter of glue line A is 3±0.5 mm.

The diameter of glue line B is 5±0.5 mm.

The distance between the center of the strip and the inner edge of the gluing surface is 3-5 mm.

The timing cover should be assembled within 10 minutes after gluing. If it is over 10 minutes, clean the glue line and apply it again.

![](images/4f5a0f7832681cf84296d807a788d0a148e83c2b284d96683d28d2c62e8125d9.webp)

c. Apply Loctite 5900 sealant evenly to the contact surface of the timing cover.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_98f2fca5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The diameter of the glue line is 4-6 mm.

Tolerances for range dimensions shown in the figure are ± 0.5 mm.

The timing cover should be assembled within 10 minutes after gluing. If it is over 10 minutes, clean the glue line and apply it again.

d. Install the housing mounting guide pin. Housing mounting guide pin: 4114870593

![](images/423bc0827469f21a5f446ddadb62ef1be352ef494fdb7314bf4924f6ebbab07a.webp)

e. Install the new O-ring into the corresponding ring slot on the cylinder head.

### Caution

The sealing ring is a disposable part, and should be replaced with a new one. Pay attention to lubricating the sealing ring before installation.

f. Move the timing cover to the installation position.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_ed40d150` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Check to confirm whether the crankshaft timing sprocket wheel end face buttons are in place.

g. Pre-tighten and fasten the fixing bolts 1-21 of timing cover in the order shown in the figure.
Bolt M8 x 30 torque: 25 N·m
Bolt M10 x 1.25 torque: 40 N·m
Bolt M10 x 1.25–10.9 levels torque: 65 N·m

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_a40ca1aa` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Specifications of bolts in the figure: bolts 9-21 are M8 x 30, bolts 4-8 are M10 x 1.25, bolts 1-3 are M10 x 1.25 10.9 grade.

After tightening all bolts, re-tighten the bolts of No.5 – 6 – 7 – 8.

![](images/a187a16e902bebed983b373cc63abcdc903d1f3ef98b10879ba19788ed3461f9.webp)

h. Connect the 3 harness clips B connecting the engine harness and the timing cover. i. Connect the harness connector A connecting the engine harness and the electronic oil pump

### 2.5.7.14 Replacement of timing chain
`geely_coolray_en_38f6f8b5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Removal procedure

1 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
2 Lift the vehicle. Refer to Lifting and Jacking of Vehicle
3 Remove the timing cover. Refer to Replacement of timing cover Remove the upper guide rail of the timing chain. Refer to Replacement of timing chain upper guide rail
5 Remove the timing chain guide rail. Refer to Replacement of timing chain guide rail
6 Remove the timing chain

![](images/626adaeeb5f9ba8c774931c54d3bc54c4554f88c14471b999e246c6398e075e2.webp)

a. Remove the timing chain.

b. Remove the crankshaft timing sprocket wheel.

Installation procedure

![](images/b877dddb282ebae5be34696f9d32067cc2da7bf75d1b4a8a68f1da93da1beec7.webp)

1 Install the timing chain.

a. Rotate the crankshaft so that the notch on the crankshaft is vertically upward (purpose: to avoid valve collision with the piston when rotating the camshaft).

![](images/6081531feb969948e7084922168754e79b25d5e6c36b73adc854766f8927c0b8.webp)

b. Adjust the position of the intake and exhaust camshaft assembly so that the camshaft tread of cylinder on the intake and exhaust camshaft is placed in an inner 8-shape position.

![](images/3ae8b5d181812c595d5ec671f73a95d41f5d9585e76b278dfa569eddaf109647.webp)

c. Install the crankshaft timing sprocket wheel, align and mesh the crankshaft timing sprocket wheel end face buttons with the crankshaft notch. d. Rotate the notch on the crankshaft parallel to the bottom surface of the cylinder block, with the notch horizontally to the left (exhaust side), as shown in the figure, when the piston is at top dead center of cylinder 1.

e. Move the timing chain to the installation position. f. Align the blue mark point A on the timing chain with the timing mark point B on the crankshaft timing sprocket wheel.

g. Align the yellow mark point A on the timing chain with the timing mark point B on the exhaust VVT assembly and the timing mark point C on the intake VVT assembly
respectively.
h. After the timing chain is assembled, check whether the timing mark points are aligned again.

2 Install the timing chain guide rail.
3 Install the upper guide rail of the timing chain.
4 Install the timing cover.
5 Lower the vehicle.
6 Connect the negative cable of battery .

### 2.5.7.15 Replacement of timing chain guide rail Removal procedure
`geely_coolray_en_d8d61671` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
2 Lift the vehicle. Refer to Lifting and Jacking of Vehicle
3 Remove the timing cover. Refer to Replacement of timing cover
4 Remove the timing chain guide rail a. Remove the 2 fixing bolts connecting the timing chain guide rail and the cylinder block. b. Remove the timing chain guide rail.

![](images/8f13f65b550258b9572d69eb1f2ade14987c75cdf9ae9154a1a7e361c4fdc683.webp)

![](images/d3dfa63c030cacb1d12a841ca00576e4568246f77ccdf2e0e9d118bcb3ae1e30.webp)

1 Install the timing chain guide rail a. Move the timing chain guide rail to the installation position.

b. Install and tighten the 2 fixing bolts connecting the timing chain guide rail and the cylinder block.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_dc8bb190` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The timing chain guide rail, the timing chain upper guide rail, and the timing chain tensioning rail of the same engine must be used in a complete set. Components from different suppliers shall not be installed on the same engine.

Install the timing cover.

### 2.5.7.18 Timing chain check

Inspection procedure

Dismount the timing gear chain. Refer to Replacement of Timing Gear Chain

2 Timing chain check

a. Tighten the timing chain with a torque of 147 N·m (metric system)/103.25 lb-ft (British system). b. Use a vernier caliper to measure the length of 15 links. Maximum length of chain: 136.36 mm (metric system) 5.368 in (British system)

![](images/1df7c7ab67fa06ed9983f4699487655d7c25d42ef6a6b3d9a7d601f3efec4a57.webp)

### Caution

Perform three random measurements. If the length is greater than the maximum value, the timing chain should be replaced.

![](images/b4cf6701d2fbf8f9969c94f0605f95f759c59e70a21874886527756ceba16567.webp)

![](images/54d8cd76cb2f80bd779bcceb436d5258a4e19b6e8f5520996ea4a0c999de3a22.webp)

Install intake and exhaust camshaft assembly a. Apply an appropriate amount of lubrication oil (i.e., engine oil) to the camshaft bearing seat at the cylinder head end. b. Apply grease completely and evenly to the 1st, 5th, and 6th journal of the intake camshaft assembly A. b. Apply grease completely and evenly to the 1st, 5th, and 6th journal of the exhaust camshaft assembly B.

d. Place the intake and exhaust camshaft assemblies on the camshaft bearing seats of the cylinder head respectively.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_a00aa733` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Check the appearance quality of the intake and exhaust camshaft assembly to ensure that the camshaft mounting surface is free of defects such as bumps, scratches, burrs and rust spots, and confirm that oil passages are not blocked.

e. Then apply a small amount of lubrication oil to the remaining journals of the camshaft and the cam surface.

f. Check whether the roller rocker arm is installed in place again.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_a00aa733` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Check the appearance quality of the intake and exhaust camshaft assembly to ensure that the camshaft mounting surface is free of defects such as bumps, scratches, burrs and rust spots, and confirm that oil passages are not blocked.

h. Spray modified alcohol or similar medium on the clean white cloth or spray it directly on the adhesive joint surface and then wipe the surface.

i. After the modified alcohol or the similar medium evaporates, apply Loctite 5900 sealant on the top surface of the cylinder head. The diameter of the glue line is (1.5 ± 0.5) mm. The distance between the center of the glue line and the cylinder head edge is (3 ± 1) mm.

j. Remove residual glue.

k. Install the camshaft rear bearing cap 1, the camshaft front bearing cap 2, the high-pressure oil pump seat 3 and the camshaft bearing cap 4.

l. Pre-tighten all bolts until the flange surface of the bolt fits the mounting surface of the bolt hole in the order shown in the figure.

m. Tighten all 26 fixing bolts in the order shown in the figure.

Torque: 13 N·m

Caution

There is no tightening or disassembly sequence requirements for the same serial number.

n. Re-tighten the 10 M8 bolts of the camshaft front bearing cap, high-pressure oil pump seat and camshaft rear bearing cap in the order shown in the figure.

### Caution

![](images/22e650e2c42788b9f0bed53f3d3bab81664972e8b5a15c3c851e92b1d0f8bea5.webp)

When installing the crankshaft rear bearing cap and the high-pressure oil pump seat, ensure that the glued surface is clean.

o. Use special tools to install the camshaft plug cover. Special tool: 4114870395

Complete the installation of the camshaft rear bearing cap and high-pressure oil pump seat and the tightening of bolts within 10 minutes after gluing.

p. Install and tighten the 1 fixing bolt 2 connecting the expansion tank return pipe and the electronic water pump. q. Install and tighten the 1 fixing bolt connecting the expansion tank return pipe and the cylinder head.

![](images/7bb53d9a483bbb759b685c22f3320fc381ec894ed988cef2ef1b256effc0cc06.webp)

1 Install the cylinder head subassembly.

a. Spray modified alcohol or similar medium on the clean white cloth or directly spray it on the adhesive joint surface to clean the contact surface between the cylinder block and the cylinder head.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_cf722c12` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before assembly, confirm whether there are collisions or scratches on the bottom surface of the cylinder head and the top surface of the cylinder block; scratches, notches, twist and stains are not allowed on the cylinder gasket, the coating is not allowed to fall off; the water holes, oil holes, etc.shall not be blocked after the cylinder head is assembled, the sealant squeezed out of the three joint surfaces or the front end needs to be scraped.

b. Apply Loctite 5900 sealant at position A on the top of the cylinder block with a diameter of 3 mm to 5 mm. The glue line starts from the front end of the cylinder block and the glue track shall be U-shaped.

c. Place the cylinder gasket on the top surface of the cylinder block, with the side with the permanent mark facing up.

d. After installing the cylinder gasket, apply Loctite 5900 sealant at position A shown on the cylinder gasket with a diameter of 3 mm to 5 mm. The glue line starts from the front end of the cylinder gasket and the glue track shall be U-shaped.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_de9baec8` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

### Caution

f. Install and tighten the 10 fixing bolts connecting the cylinder head subassembly and the cylinder block in the order of 1-10 shown in Figure.

The bolt of the cylinder head is a disposable part, and must be replaced with a new one after each removal

When tightening the bolts, tighten the single bolt multiple times, and tighten according to the specified torque.

Torque:

First time 35 N·m

Second time: 90°

Third time: 120°

j. Move the degassing hose to the installation position. k. Install the 1 clamp A connecting the degassing hose and the cylinder head.
l. Move the warm air water inlet pipe to the installation position.
m. Install and tighten the 2 fixing bolts connecting the warm air water inlet pipe and the cylinder head.
Torque: 10 N·m n. Move the water outlet pipe of the expansion tank to the installation position.
o. Install and tighten the fixing bolt 2 connecting the water outlet pipe of the expansion tank with the cylinder head subassembly.
Torque: 10 N·m
p. Move the supercharger oil inlet pipe to the installation position.
q. Install and tighten the fixing bolt 1 connecting the supercharger oil inlet pipe and the cylinder head
subassembly.
Torque: 45 N·m a. Connect the A/C warm air water outlet pipe and the expansion tank water outlet pipe.
s. Install the 1 clamp B connecting the A/C warm air water outlet pipe and the expansion tank water outlet pipe. t. Connect the A/C warm air water inlet pipe and the warm air water inlet pipe hard pipe.

2.5.7.23 Replacement of vacuum pump Removal procedure

1 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
2 Remove engine trim cover. Refer to Replacement of engine trim cover
3 Remove the canister solenoid valve c/w pipeline Refer to Replacement of canister solenoid valve c/w pipeline Remove the air filter corrugated pipe. Refer to Replacement of air filter corrugated pipe
5 Remove the vacuum pump

![](images/811641f8ee92136706eb72690a2e4c4385e22d6694797816f4ffffc88de2f72d.webp)

a. Remove the 2 fixing bolts 1 connecting the canister solenoid valve bracket and the vacuum pump. b. Remove the 1 fixing bolt 2 connecting the engine harness and the canister solenoid valve bracket. c. Disconnect the double-pipe clip A from the canister solenoid valve bracket. d. Remove the canister solenoid valve bracket.

e. Disconnect the quick connector connecting the vacuum pipe and the vacuum pump.

f. Remove the 3 fixing bolts connecting the vacuum pump and the cylinder head.
g. Remove the vacuum pump.

### Installation procedure
`geely_coolray_en_747e5fce` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

![](images/b6aae43fe337ab05c962b6fd5941ecffacedebf9df3419680abd91f2cea2514f.webp)

![](images/8fa53f7d3978af2e4e69f4b8ee78501fa50c9e5e5b06baaf8cf3b65f1e0b5caa.webp)

1 Install the vacuum pump a. Clean the vacuum pump mounting surface. b. Apply Loctite 5900 glue as shown in the figure.

c. Replace the vacuum pump sealing ring.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_0690f34a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The sealing ring cannot be reused. It must be replaced with a new one after each removal.

![](images/6b7b73255ce48750a2a27bde1ad671496f70eec945cdadc3d14812c06dd39e28.webp)

b. Install and tighten the 3 fixing bolts connecting the vacuum pump and the cylinder head. Torque: 16 N·m

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_78676758` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Confirm that the sealing ring on the vacuum pump assembly is installed correctly and that the vacuum pump connector can rotate normally without catching. Align the vacuum pump coupling with the groove at the end of the camshaft to assemble it on the cylinder head.

e. Connect the quick connector connecting the vacuum pipe and the vacuum pump.

f. Connect the double-pipe clip A and the canister
solenoid valve bracket.
g. Install and tighten the 1 fixing bolt 2 connecting the engine harness and the canister solenoid valve bracket. h. Install and tighten the 2 fixing bolts 1 connecting the canister solenoid valve bracket and the vacuum pump. Torque: 10 N·m

2 Install the air filter corrugated pipe.
3 Install the canister solenoid valve c/w pipeline.
4 Install engine trim cover.
5 Connect the negative cable of battery.

3. When installing PCV valve, it is necessary to apply thread tightening glue to the thread part of PCV valve (Tianshan 1243).

4. The glue requirements are shown in the figure.

2 Install the crankcase ventilation pipe.

### 2.7.1.3 Content description of catalytic converter label
`geely_coolray_en_fb703c87` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

A label including manufacturer and model information is pasted on the outer surface of a three-way catalytic converter with its appearance and content are shown in the following figure:

![](images/3f63834ad5cb0c4040ecfc95bcbef243b55f2e20671a7e7739585010ce4036c8.webp)

SC: Refer to assembly manufacturer, for example: FAURECIA; HT stands for Chongqing Hiter; SEJONG stands for Taicang Sejong Auto Parts Co.,; KESEN stands for Ningbo Kesen.

FZ: Refer to packaging enterprise, for example: FAURECIA; HT stands for Chongqing Hiter; SEJONG stands for Taicang Sejong Auto Parts Co.,; KESEN stands for Ningbo Kesen.

TC: Refer to coating manufacturer, for example: JM stands for Johnson Matthey; WFLD stands for Wuxi Weifu LIDA Catalytic Converter Co., Ltd.; KESEN stands for Ningbo Kesen; BASF stands for BASF SE.

ZT: Refer to carrier manufacturer, for example: CORNING; NGK.

### 2.7.1.4 Three-way Catalytic Converter
`geely_coolray_en_a0dd76f1` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Exhaust Manifold

Cylinder head integrated exhaust manifold is adopted for this engine. The cylinder head integrated exhaust manifold allows the engine to reach normal temperature faster in the cold starting state. Since the exhaust manifold is located in the cylinder head with a cooling pipeline, the exhaust temperature of engine when the vehicle is at high speed and high load can be effectively reduced, so that the exhaust gas flows to the turbine at a lower temperature, achieving higher efficiency and reducing the turbo lag.

Turbo charger

Turbocharger is mainly used to increase air intake pressure. Exhaust drives the impellers in the turbocharger to rotate at high speed, increasing the intake pressure and forcing more air to enter the combustion chamber.

Three-way catalytic converter assembly

Three-way catalytic converter assembly-the front is mainly used to reduce harmful gases and hydrocarbons in the exhaust. Catalytic converter-the active materials in the front include platinum, palladium and rhodium. The converter combines carbon monoxide (CO) with unburnt hydrocarbons (HC) to generate carbon dioxide (C2) and water (HO). The converter can also reduce nitrogen oxides (NOx). The front and rear oxygen sensors are located in the three-way catalytic converter assembly and are used to measure the oxygen content in the front and rear of the three-way catalytic converter assembly.

A ceramic carrier in a honeycomb shape along the exhaust direction is arranged in the stainless steel housing. The ceramic carrier is surrounded by a gasket. The main function of the gasket is to fix the ceramic carrier to prevent any contact and collision with the inner shell.

Muffler assembly

The muffler housing is in the slotted structure, and the muffler housing, exhaust pipe and flange are welded together, forming the rear muffler assembly. The muffler is used to reduce exhaust noise.

Differential pressure sensor

The differential pressure sensor is used to detect the pressure change of the GPF. The collected particulate matter will be temporarily stored in the GPF, if the particulate matter continues to increase, it will affect the exhaust efficiency. If the particulate matter is not handled at the appropriate time, the vehicle performance may be influenced and the GPF may be damaged. The pressure difference between the GPF intake and exhaust can be detected by the sensor. Therefore, the differential pressure sensor is also called the particulate filter pressure sensor.

### 2.7.3.1 System working principles
`geely_coolray_en_dfa10597` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The surface of the ceramic carrier in the three-way catalytic converter exposed to the exhaust gas is coated with a layer of catalyst. The catalyst contains three precious metals: platinum, palladium and rhodium. These catalysts play a role in promoting chemical reactions.

A catalyst is a substance that accelerates a chemical reaction without changing itself. Exhaust of the engine contains carbon monoxide (CO), hydrocarbons (HC) and nitrogen oxides (NOMA). When the exhaust gas flows through the ceramic carrier, a chemical reaction takes place in the three-way catalytic converter. Carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons are oxidized by the oxygen (O2S) in the exhaust gas and converted into carbon dioxide (CO2S) and water vapor (H2O). Nitrogen oxides are converted into nitrogen (N2S) through the reduction reaction with carbon monoxide. This three-way catalytic converter can simultaneously convert the three components (CO, HC, and NOAN) in the exhaust gas into harmless neutral gas, thus is called the three-type converter.

The GPF rear catalytic converter is composed of honeycomb ceramics with a certain hole density. Exhaust gas can alternately block the honeycomb porous ceramic filter, and the exhaust gas is forced to pass through the wall of the hole. The particles are filtered by diffusion, stopping, gravity and inertia. When the particles accumulate to a certain degree, GPF regeneration will be triggered, and the trapped carbon particles and oxygen will be oxidized and consumed.

The muffler consumes the energy of the exhaust gas flow and balances the pressure fluctuation of the airflow, thereby eventually reducing the exhaust noise.

### 2.7.6.1 Diagnosis description
`geely_coolray_en_e180fc98` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before diagnosing the fault of the exhaust system, refer to Description and Operations Understand and get familiar with exhaust system working principle before system diagnosis. This helps to determine the correct fault diagnosis steps when a trouble occurs. More importantly, it also helps to determine whether the situation described by the distributor is normal. Any fault diagnosis of the exhaust system should start with a routine inspection that guides the serviceman to take the next logical step for troubleshooting. Understanding and using the diagnosis flow chart correctly can shorten the time of diag nosis and avoid misjudgment of the faulty part.

### 2.7.6.2 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_758e3182` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Check after-sales installations that may affect exhaust system operation. Make sure these installations cannot affect normal operation of the exhaust system.

Check system components that are easily accessible or can be seen to find out if there is any obvious damage of the component or there is a situation that may cause a fault.

Check the color of exhaust gas in the exhaust pipe to judge whether the system is normal.

### 2.7.6.3 Exhaust System Is Blocked
`geely_coolray_en_3132e6d8` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

When the engine has power loss, poor fuel economy or poor acceleration performance, it is necessary to check whether there is an "exhaust system blockage" fault. The possible causes for exhaust system blockage are:

The exhaust pipes are damaged.

There is debris in the exhaust pipes.

Internal fault of muffler or resonator.

The interior of the exhaust pipes rust and blank plug the exhaust outlet.

-Three-way catalytic converter is blocked.

-GPF catalytic converter is blocked.

Warning！

Refer to Warnings and Precautions

Warning！

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_35a5a0fe` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The three-way catalytic converter assembly may be damaged or fail if the following conditions occur: Its work exceeds the limits of the closed-loop gas mixture control system.
The engine burns a lot of engine oil.
The temperature of the exhaust gas at the three-way catalytic converter is too high, exceeding 840°C (1,5

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_ae787cff` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Vehicles with a three-way catalytic converter assembly cannot use leaded gasoline. Lead will contaminate the three-way catalytic converter assembly.
Never drop the three-way catalytic converter assembly, as this may damage the ceramic carrier.
Do not allow water, engine oil or fuel to enter the converter, as this may contaminate the ceramic carrier.
Do not start the vehicle when the engine is misfired or the ignition coil units are disconnected.

### 2.7.6.8 Tightness inspection of smoke tester
`geely_coolray_en_e09e9795` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:body | p:1

Troubleshooting Guide for Smoke Tester
![](images/364ff199727d768c5fa3320850ce0b5c7cf82c8a3103a4be0452b226405bb789.webp)

1. The smoke leakage tester can be used for nearly any low-pressure system of a vehicle suspected to have a leak, such as the fuel evaporative emission control system, air intake/exhaust system, and vacuum system, and can also be used to search for the leakage position of doors windows, and sunroof sealing strips. In addition, the function tests and unit tests of solenoid valves can be used.

Optional air source

1. Since the gas provided is an inactive gas, this gas pack makes the 4114720215 leakage tester very portable and very suitable for safe EVAP tests. 1L of nitrogen dioxide in the gas cylinder can perform a complete test cycle of 25 times (125 minutes), and it is very economical to refill it. Please note that for safety reasons, the cylinder is empty when delivered. Before first-time use, contact the local nitrogen dioxide filling station to add liquid nitrogen dioxide.

Smoke generating solution

1. The patented solution is the only smoke generating solution approved by an automobile manufacturer. The chemical in the solution contains a special dye that can be deposited at the exact location of the leak. Each bottle of solution can perform about 300 complete tests. (12 ounces/ 355 ml). 4114720215 is equipped with a bottle of solution. Parts No. F00E900348760 is one bottle.

### Basic test process
`geely_coolray_en_964e50cb` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:body | p:1

1. Connect a 4114720215 leakage tester to an air supply of 6 bar/8 bar. 2. Add the wire clamp of the 4114720215 leakage tester to the positive and negative poles of the vehicle battery. Considering that there may be sparks when the clamp is clamped to the negative pole of the battery, it is necessary to reliably ground the negative clamp with the vehicle body. 3. Observe the green power supply indicator lamp on the 4114720215 leakage tester. If the green lamp is on, confirm that the connection is correct. Flashing of the green power supply indicator lamp indicates low battery level. 4. Turn to the smoke mode, and according to the system to be tested, select the appropriate adapter, connect the adapter to the vehicle pipeline, and then connect the smoke outlet pipe to the air inlet of the adapter. The flow control valve must be in the fully opened (+) position. 5. Press the power button, the red indicator lamp is on, the device starts to work, and the smoke generated will be injected into the system to be measured. A test cycle is 5 minutes, and the device will turn off automatically after 5 minutes. 6. Use the white light of the attached electric torch to find the leaked smoke. When smoke is found, use ultraviolet light to illuminate at the leakage position to find the fluoresce light. The fluoresce position is the leakage position. stem test description

EVAP sy

When the oil level in the vehicle fuel tank is lower than the fuel filler, the best test effect can be achieved

1. Connect the equipment to 6 bar-8 bar of inactive compressed gas, and turn the flow control valve to the maximum position.
2. Press the switch button, and when the smoke comes out from the smoke outlet, connect the smoke outlet pipe of the tester to the EVAP system.

Generally, EVAP systems are connected from two locations:

1. Connect from the fuel filler cap, put the fuel tank cap adapter over the fuel filler cap, and connect the smoke outlet pipe to the fuel tank cap adapter.
2. Connect from the desorption pipe of the canister, disconnect the quick joint of the desorption pipe, connect a three-way joint of suitable size, and connect the smoke outlet pipe to the three-way joint. It is recommended to connect from the canister desorption pipeline, because the fuel filler cap is prone to leak, so the leakage of the fuel filler cap is eliminated by connecting from the fuel tank cap.

3. If smoke is introduced into the EVAP system, do not close the canister exhaust valve or unscrew the fuel filler cap. Keep the system open and let the smoke escape out of the opening so as to confirm that the system is clear and has been completely filled with smoke. If the flow ball drops below mm when the system is open, it indicates that the system is not smooth and is blocked. If it drops directly to the bottom, it indicates that the system is completely blocked.

4. When smoke escapes from the opening, close the canister exhaust valve or tighten the fuel filler cap, and continue to fill the system with smoke. When the pressure rises to 32 mbar or the flow ball stops falling and stabilizes in a certain position, it indicates that the system is full

### Basic test process
`geely_coolray_en_8ba7bbce` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

5. When the system is full and the tester is still working, check the stably parked position of the flow ball and check which interval of the three reference leakage points on the flow meter it is to determine whether the system is qualified or not. If the flow ball drops to the bottom, it indicates that there is no leakage in the system.
6. If the flow ball is lower than 0.25 mm, it may not be repaired, and if the flow ball is higher than 0.25 mm, repair is recommended. Use the white light of the electric torch to check the components of the EVAP system. When the smoke leaks out, reduce the smoke flow to locate the leakage position, switch to the ultraviolet light, and the deposited fluoresce agent can be seen at the leakage position. If the leakage point is small and the smoke leakage is not obvious, switch to the laser and irradiate the suspected area. When the laser beam is found, it indicate a leak, move the electric torch left and right. The laser beam is shorted to the leakage direction, and then switch to ultraviolet light to search for fluoresce position.
7. If the leakage is below 0.5 mm, no smoke leakage is found, but the fault lamp is on, it may be an internal leak, a fault in the circuit or parts, or an intermittent leakage. For internal leakages, disassemble the parts. Faults of circuit and parts need to be judged by reading the waveform with a diagnostic apparatus. For intermittent leakages, pull the connecting pipelines of each part by hand during the test to see if the flow ball bounces. For example, pulling a pipe or part, and the flow ball bounces up, it indicates that there is intermittent leakage.
8. For leaks below 0.5 mm, it is difficult to find the leakage point from the whole system, and it can be detected in sections. Divide the system into fuel tank section, carbon tank section and desorption section through threeway joints, test the leakage amount of each section respectively to reduce the scope of inspection. If no smoke or fluoresce light is found, remove suspected parts for individual testing, and gradually reduce the test range.

### Warning！
`geely_coolray_en_fdf932bc` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:fuel_ev | p:1

When testing the EVAP system, SAE international paper [SAE: 2007-01-1235 and 2008-01-0554] strongly recommends that any test equipment, including any leakage tester, must use an inert gas source such as nitrogen or CO2. The air introduced into the fuel tank will form a flammable air-fuel mixture inside the fuel tank. The air contains 21% oxygen, and only 12% oxygen is required for flammable mixture. If the workshop environment outside the fuel tank is full of potential sources of fire, such as sparks generated by the release of static electricity, the fuel tank can be ignited. In addition, many fuel tanks nowadays have electric fuel pump systems and some harnesses, which are all dangerous sources. Therefore, when testing the EVAP system, be sure to use a safe operation method.

### 2.8.1.2 Cooling System Specification
`geely_coolray_en_9d01e70d` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Electronic water pump

![](images/1eabd494b08a9e04957b436f9fb2739df6534ca70341c32255ffae2575dff443.webp)

Thermostat casing components

![](images/f683498f093e22a7e274622854787555adda932239464c7a6ddd2cf255cd0074.webp)

### Introduction to the role and operation of cooling system
`geely_coolray_en_e8c199e1` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

When the engine is working, it distributes the heat absorbed by the components to the atmosphere in time and in an appropriate amount, so as to maintain the engine at a suitable operating temperature; in addition, when the ambient temperature is low, the cooling system has the function of ensuring the engine to quickly warm up.

The engine coolant temperature sensor measures the temperature of the coolant. ECM uses the measurement result to control multiple functions, such as fan speed. When the engine is overheated, the driver will see prompt information on the instrument pack.

When the engine is working, the gas mixture is burned in the cylinder combustion chamber to generate high temperature, and the heat is transferred through the cylinder block. If the temperature is not reduced, the engine will stop working. Therefore, an engine coolant channel is provided in the cylinder body to exchange heat with the outside world through the circulation of the engine coolant. In this way, the working temperature of the engine can be kept within a certain range, so that the engine can work effectively under all working conditions.

When the engine is cold, the cooling system controls the circulation of engine coolant through the thermostat, which can quickly warm up the engine. The cooling system includes a radiator, an expansion tank assembly, an engine cooling fan, a thermostat and its casing, and an electronic water pump. The electronic water pump is controlled by the ECM and runs at different speeds according to the signals sent by the ECM. Only when the above functions are performed normally can the cooling system work normally.

When the engine coolant reaches the working temperature of the thermostat, the thermostat opens. At this point, the engine coolant returns to the radiator and gets cooled. The cooling system introduces part of the engine coolant into the heater core through the water pipe for heating and defrosting.

When the cooling system is in the cold state, the engine coolant level should be maintained between the MIN (minimum) and MAX (maximum) marks on the expansion tank assembly. The cooling fan assembly is installed at the rear of the radiator in the engine compartment. It can increase the ventilation of the radiator and the air-conditioning condenser, thereby helping to increase the cooling speed of the vehicle at idle or low speed.

Warning！

As long as there is pressure in the cooling system, even if the solution in the radiator is not boiling, the solution temperature will be much higher than the boiling temperature. If the pressure cap is opened when the engine is not cooled and the pressure is still high, the coolant will immediately boil and may generate explosive force, spraying on the engine, fenders and the person who opens the radiator pressure cap.

The cooling system is mainly composed of radiator, cooling fan, radiator inlet and outlet pipes, expansion tank assembly, thermostat and so on.

The automatic transmission has an independent cooling system used to cool down the automatic transmission oil. The system is mainly composed of oil cooler components, and its basic working principle is consistent with that of engine water cooling system.

### Thermostat
`geely_coolray_en_de8c4668` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The function of the thermostat is to control the flow of engine coolant in the cooling system. The thermostat prevents the engine coolant from flowing from the engine to the radiator, allowing the engine to quickly warm up and adjusting the engine coolant temperature. When the engine coolant temperature is low, the thermostat remains in the closed position, preventing the engine coolant from circulating through the radiator. At this time, only the engine coolant is allowed to circulate through the heater core, thereby quickly and uniformly warming up the engine. When the engine warms up, the thermostat opens. Allow engine coolant to flow through the radiator and dissipate heat through the radiator. The opening and closing of the thermostat will allow enough engine coolant to enter the radiator to keep the engine within the normal operating temperature range.

### Cooling fan
`geely_coolray_en_dcb24e0a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The electronic engine cooling fan is mainly used to provide additional air flow through the radiator and condenser. The engine cooling fan sends signals to ECM and is controlled by ECM. The engine cooling fan speed is determined according to the cooling demand. The engine cooling fan is directly connected to ECM.

### Warning！
`geely_coolray_en_59e6a0e6` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Even when the engine is not running, the electronic fan under the engine compartment hood may also start and hurt people. Keep hands, clothes and tools away from the electronic fan under the engine compartment hood.

Warning！

If the fan blades are bent or damaged to any degree, do not repair or reuse damaged parts. Bending or damaged fan blades must be replaced. Damaged fan blades cannot guarantee normal balance and may malfunction and fly off during continuous use. This is very dangerous.

### Take out expansion tank assembly.
`geely_coolray_en_7d703e4f` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The main function of the expansion tank assembly is to provide an expansion space for the coolant to remove the air trapped in the coolant and the water vapor generated at the high temperature of the engine in time, so as to make more effective use of the heat dissipation function of the radiator and improve the cooling efficiency.

### Radiator
`geely_coolray_en_943fb5b8` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The main function of the radiator is to reduce the temperature of the engine coolant. The main method is to provide more contact area with the outside world for the overheated coolant, so that the wind blown by the cooling fan during operation can take away the heat of the coolant to the greatest extent.

### 2.8.6.1 Diagnosis description
`geely_coolray_en_629549cd` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before diagnosing the faults of the cooling system, refer to Instructions and Operations and System Operating Principle. Understand and be familiar with the working principle of the cooling system before system diagnosis. This helps to determine correct fault diagnosis steps when a fault occurs. More importantly, it also helps to determine whether the situation described by the distributor is normal. Understanding and using the diagnosis flow chart correctly can shorten the time of diagnosis and avoid misjudgment of the faulty part.

### 2.8.6.2 Cooling Fan Circuit Diagnosis
`geely_coolray_en_71912864` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:electrical | p:1

Hints:

• If the user reports an overheating trouble, first confirm whether the trouble is the boiling of the engine coolant or that the engine coolant temperature gauge indicates overheating. If the engine does overheat but the cooling fan is still running normally, the engine cooling system should be checked at this time.

• If ECM has just controlled the relay to pull in, the cooling fan fuse in the engine fuse box will blow, then there may be a short circuit to ground between the fan relay and the fan motor grounding, and the cooling fan motor may be short-circuited.

• You can use the "function test" in the scan tool to force the high and low speed relays of the cooling fan to pull in and check whether the fan can work normally to quickly determine the trouble.

### Caution

Be sure the coolant is always present in the expansion tank. In case the coolant thermometer shows that the temperature is too high, close the engine and cool it down.

2.8.7.8 Replacement of electronic water pump Removal procedure

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_fd46ee6d` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Do not perform this operation when the coolant is hot to avoid burns.

Special hoop pliers should be used when removing or installing water pipe hoop.

Before disconnecting the water pipes, please place a container under the vehicle to catch the antifreeze to avoid contaminating the ground.

After the pipeline is disconnected, the pipeline should be wrapped in time to prevent foreign objects from entering the pipeline.

1 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable

2 Drain the engine coolant. Refer to Discharge and Filling of Engine Coolant

3 Remove the supercharger intake muffler. Refer to Replacement of supercharger intake muffler

4 Remove the thermostat casing components. Refer to Replacement of thermostat casing components

5 Remove the electronic water pump

![](images/be52edc91f96a85b44594e47f8baa76bc3fefae76dbbe87fbf0a0c4b683d113d.webp)

a. Disconnect the harness connector A connecting the engine harness and the electronic water pump.
b. Remove the 1 fixing clamp B connecting the electronic water pump and the rubber pipe.
c. Disconnect the electronic water pump from the rubber pipe.
d. Remove the 1 fixing clamp C connecting the electronic water pump and the degassing hose.
e. Disconnect the electronic water pump from the
degassing hose. f. Remove the 1 fixing clamp B connecting the electronic water pump and the water return pipe of the oil cooler. g. Disconnect the electronic water pump from the oil cooler return pipe.
h. Remove the 1 fixing clamp A connecting the electronic water pump and the hose.
i. Disconnect the electronic water pump from the hose.

![](images/6f30b6a1ec8e59824c80626219c8871e615cef2204ab16b624ec96383cf16964.webp)

j. Remove the 2 fixing bolts connecting the electronic water pump and the cylinder block.

k. Remove the T fixing bolt 1 connecting the expansion tank water return pipe and the electronic water pump. l. Remove the fixing bolt 2 connecting the electronic water pump and the cylinder head. m. Remove the fixing bolt 3 connecting the warm air water inlet pipe and the electronic water pump. n. Remove the electronic water pump.

### Installation procedure
`geely_coolray_en_ad99c8ad` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1 Install the electronic water pump

![](images/04d016e87d855cef90995c908fe12dafa9fe8cc39df42cf1fe6ee12b375ab608.webp)

a. Move the electronic water pump to the installation position.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_8bfb3837` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. The gasket is not reusable. It must be replaced with a new one after every removal

2. Check for scratches or impurities on the inner wall of the water outlet of the electronic water pump and the sealing ring of the water inlet pipe of the water pump, and apply P80 lubricant on the two places evenly.

3. Press the electronic water pump horizontally into the water inlet pipe of the pump to ensure that the sealing ring does not squeeze out.

b. Pre-tighten the bolts in the order of 2-3-1 as shown in figure, and then tighten the fixing bolts of the electronic water pump components in the order of 1-2-3 as shown in figure.

Torque: 25 N m

![](images/34443b7b9881361476a9bf80d7f938b6c7e20df7414ebcb6b8fe0460649fd2e1.webp)

c. Install and tighten the 1 fixing bolt 2 connecting the electronic water pump and the cylinder head.
Torque: 10 N m
d. Install and tighten the fixing bolt connecting the expansion tank water return pipe and the electronic water pump.

Torque: 10 N m

e. Connect the electronic water pump with the hose. f. Install the 1 fixing clamp A connecting the electronic water pump and the hose.

### Caution

### 2.9.1.2 Lubricating System Specifications
`geely_coolray_en_ec93fb40` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Electronic oil pump

![](images/73029d908faa38f4fe0998feb99b40ac77df281866245a0ce7eeb1958d7dcf69.webp)

Oil pressure sensor

![](images/ad481128e8aa1a487324cdf2bfd57e5e70bf67941923f1fe0e4e494300e1befd.webp)

### 2.9.2.1 Instructions and Operations
`geely_coolray_en_3623a86f` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Oil pan

The oil pan is mainly used to collect engine oil. There is an oil drain plug on the oil pan. The oil drain plug is located at the bottom of the oil pan and is used to drain engine oil.

The engine oil pan is installed at the bottom of the crankcase. The oil pump draws engine oil from the oil pan. After passing the oil filter element, the engine oil passes through the oil passage to lubricate the cylinder block and cylinder head respectively. The engine oil passes through the engine oil passage in the crankshaft to the crankshaft connecting rod, then to the piston and cylinder, and finally returns to the oil pan. Some of the lubrication oil flows to the turbo charger sub-assembly through the specific oil passage for lubrication of the turbo charger sub-assembly and finally returns to the oil pan. In the second oil passage, the engine oil passes through the engine oil passage to the camshaft, and the engine oil passes through the internal oil passage of the camshaft to lubricate the valve assembly and finally return to the oil pan.

Engine oil pump

The oil pump draws engine oil from the oil pan, and then delivers the engine oil to each part of the engine with pressure. The oil pump draws engine oil from the oil pan and delivers it to each part of the engine. A oil suction filter subassembly component is installed at the oil pump inlet, and the oil suction filter subassembly component filters through the impurities in the oil. The oil pump is driven by the concave surface of the crankshaft, so as long as the crankshaft rotates, the oil pump will also participate in the work. Because the fixed-displacement oil pump is used, when the engine speed is high, the output pressure of the oil pump will exceed the demand of the engine's lubricating system. Therefore, a pressure limiting valve is provided on the electronic oil pump. The pressure relief chamber of the pressure limiting valve is connected to the oil inlet chamber of the oil pump. When the output pressure exceeds a certain degree, the pressure limiting valve opens and the excess oil flows back to the oil pump inlet chamber through the pressure limiting valve. During normal oil supply, the pressure limiting valve keeps the bypass closed.

Engine oil filter element module

The oil filter element module is mainly used to clean engine oil. Engine oil flows from the oil pan to the oil filter element module. Engine oil passes through the oil filter element module to remove contaminants from the engine. The filtered engine oil flows back to the oil pan.

Engine oil cooler component

The engine oil cooler component is installed on the crankcase. The engine oil cooler component is mainly used to cool engine oil.

Lubricating instructions

After the engine oil is cooled through the engine oil cooler component, it flows upward through the oil filter element from the upper oil passage of the oil filter element seat. Engine oil flows downward through the oil passage and passes the front of the cylinder block. These oil passages supply engine oil to the oil passages of each cylinder head, main shaft passage, and left stabilizer shaft. Oil passages of each cylinder head lead engine oil into the oil control valve and hydraulic tappet. Engine oil flows from the main oil passage, through the oil control valve filter element and the oil control valve oil chamber to the VVT components. The oil control valve is used to control the inlet and exhaust VVT components. The oil control valve is controlled by the engine control module (ECM).

### 2.9.4.1 Diagnosis description
`geely_coolray_en_833c4af1` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before diagnosing the faults of the lubrication system, refer to Instructions and Operations and System Operating Principle. Understand and be familiar with the working principle of lubrication system before starting the diagnosis. This will help to determine the correct diagnosis procedures when a fault occurs. More importantly, it can also help to confirm whether the situation described by the client is subject to normal operation. Any fault diagnosis of lubrication system should start with routine examination, and guide maintenance personnel to take the next logical step to conduct fault diagnosis. Understanding and using the diagnosis flow chart correctly can shorten the time of diagnosis and avoid misjudgment of the faulty part.

### 2.9.4.2 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_2cb0f400` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Check after-sales installations that may affect lubrication system operation, to ensure these devices cannot affect the normal operation of the lubrication system.
• Check system components that are easily accessible or can be seen to find out if they are obviously clogged or whether there is leakage. If there is leak, first confirm whether it is an engine oil leak.

Check whether the oil filter is dirty or clogged and replace if necessary.

### 2.9.5.1 Drainage and filling of engine oil
`geely_coolray_en_703e1a14` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1 Lift the vehicle. Refer to Lifting and Jacking of Vehicle

2 Remove the bottom shield of the engine. Refer to Replacement of engine bottom shield
3 Put the recovery container to the bottom of the car and prepare to receive the released engine oil.
4 Unscrew the oil filler cap counterclockwise.
5 Put the recovery container position under the oil pan drain plug.
6 Remove the oil drain plug and gaskets of the oil pan, and drain the engine oil until the oil drops.
7 Install the drain plug gasket and drain plug of the oil pan. Torque: 35 N·m

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_58f935a7` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The drain bolt gasket is a disposable piece, and should be replaced with a new one after each removal.

8 Lower the vehicle and place it on level ground.
9 Fill the specified amount of oil and screw on the oil filler cap clockwise.
10 Start the vehicle and run the engine for 3 minutes to check for oil leaks.
11 Turn off the engine and wait for 10 minutes for engine oil to return to the oil pan. Caution If you do not do this, the oil dipstick may not show the actual oil level.
12 Pull out the engine oil dipstick, clean with tissue or cloth and then re-insert to the bottom.
13 Pull out engine oil dipstick again to inspect oil level; the oil level is required to be above 1/2 of the oil dipstick scale a.
14 If the engine oil level is found to be lower than the oil dipstick scale a, screw off the oil filler cap and add an appropriate amount of engine oil so that the oil level is above 1/2 of the oil dipstick scale a.
15 Start the vehicle again, run at idle speed for 3 minutes, and wait for 10 minutes after turning off the engine. Check the engine oil level again. Refill engine oil if necessary. Ensure that the engine oil level is above 1/2 of the oil dipstick scale a.

![](images/bc73434fcbd7d61735d109d8962fec931716a1aaa2edcdd7d2cf45f5b3bb7b9d.webp)

### 2.10.2.1 Instructions and Operations
`geely_coolray_en_ed68450b` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Spark plug

The spark plug is installed under the ignition coil assembly. The spark plug is mainly used to ignite the oil-gas mixture in the combustion chamber. The spark plug is connected to the ignition coil assembly, which generates a high voltage. An electric spark is generated between the positive and negative poles of the spark plug. The ignition timing is controlled by the engine control module (ECM).

Ignition coil

The ignition coil assembly is installed on the top of the engine. The ignition coil assembly supplies high voltage to the spark plug. The ignition coil assembly has an integrated voltage amplifier, which converts the 12V voltage into a high voltage of 38 kV according to the ECU instructions and provides the high voltage to the spark plug. Voltage transformation is carried out through the primary and secondary coils, magnetism is carried out through the IGBT module controlled by the ECU signal, and the discharge is controlled by a Zener diode.

### 2.10.3.1 System Operating Principles
`geely_coolray_en_81f1af7a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

When the ignition switch is in the "ON" position and ECM detects that there is a voltage in the ECM harness connector, it controls the internal grounding of the ECM, and then controls the main relay to pull in through the ECM harness connector. After the battery voltage passes through the main relay, it reaches the ignition coils of each cylinder through fuses to provide operating power to the ignition coils.

The crankshaft position sensor is a magnetic inductive speed sensor. The crankshaft position sensor signal plate is integrated with the flywheel. When the engine runs, the crankshaft position sensor signal plate also starts to rotate, thus the sensor also generates a corresponding alternating signal which is sent to ECM. ECM calculates the current crankshaft angle according to this signal to determine the benchmark where piston reaches top dead center, which directly affects the accuracy of ignition advance angle control, so this sensor signal is a vital input signal in the ignition system. When ECM cannot receive this signal, the ignition system cannot work. The ECM harness connector receives the signal input from the crankshaft position sensor, calculates the ignition advance angle, and then controls the ignition of each cylinder through the ECM harness connector.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_e00ed02a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:body | p:1

When the vehicle body anti-theft alarm system and engine anti-theft locking system are activated, ECM is prohibited to control the ignition coil, and the ignition system does not work at this time.

### 2.10.7.1 Diagnosis description
`geely_coolray_en_b90aad3d` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before diagnosing the faults of the ignition system, refer to Instructions and Operations and System Operating Principle. Understand and be familiar with working principles of ignition system before starting system diagnosis. This helps to determine the correct fault diagnosis steps when a fault occurs. More importantly, it also helps to determine whether the situation described by the customer is normal operation. Any fault diagnosis of the ignition system should start with routine inspection. The routine inspection will guide maintenance personnel to take the next logical step for fault diagnosis. Understanding and using the diagnosis flow chart correctly can shorten the time of diagnosis and avoid misjudgment of the faulty part.

### 2.10.7.2 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_6a4ef476` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Check after-sale installations that may affect the operation of the ignition system to ensure that they do not affect the operation of the ignition system.
Checking system parts that are easily accessible or can be seen to guarantee that there is no obvious damage or situation that may cause a fault.

### 2.10.7.3 Common faults of spark plugs in use
`geely_coolray_en_71ee9999` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

The spark plug is severely ablated: Scarring, damage or electrode melting or ablation on the top of the spark plug indicate that the spark plug has been damaged and should be replaced. When replacing, check the burning symptoms and the color change to analyze the cause of the fault Refer to Replacement of spark plug

1. The electrode melts and the insulator is white, indicating that the inside temperature of the combustion is too high. The reasons may be exhaust valve overheating or poor operation of cooling devices caused by excessive carbon deposits in the combustion chamber and oversize valve clearance, or because the spark plug is not tightened to the specified torque.

2. The rounded electrode and scars on the insulator indicate pre-ignition of the engine, which may be due to premature ignition, low gasoline octane value or high calorific value of the spark plug.

3. The top of the insulator is cracked. Knocking combustion is the main reason for insulator rupture, and premature ignition time, low gasoline octane value, and high temperature in the combustion chamber may all cause knocking combustion in the engine.

4. There are gray-black stripes on the top of the insulator. These stripes indicate that the spark plug has leaked gas and should be replaced with a new one.

There are deposits on the spark plug: sometimes there are deposits between the top of the spark plug insulator and the electrode, which can cause the engine to not work in severe cases. If the spark plug is cleaned, it can be temporarily rectified.

In order to maintain good performance, the cause of the trouble must be identified.

1. Oily deposits. Oily deposits on the spark plug indicate that the lubricant has entered the combustion chamber. If it is just an individual spark plug, the oil seal of the valve stem may be damaged. If spark plugs in all cylinders are stuck by such deposits, it indicates oil blow-by of the cylinders, and it is necessary to check whether the air filter and the ventilation device are blocked.

2. Black deposits. There are black deposits on the spark plug electrode and inside of it, indicating that the gas mixture is too thick.
Keep the engine running at a higher speed for a few minutes during which the black soot layer left on the electrode can be burnt.

The central electrode of the spark plug that burns fuel normally is gray or yellow.

![](images/19e500273740aaf8bd5c252a421dd5e7397e2e001322f2b8549865023cb844eb.webp)

The central electrode of the spark plug that burns fuel excessively is severely eroded.

![](images/bdbf194d924a64ddaec9f3bef5279fd2f976a8878d638afcb84d50a59c567d2b.webp)

If the spark plug calorific value is incorrect or any fault occurs due to engine fuel system fault, the central electrode of the spark plug and the central insulator will have very serious carbon deposition.

![](images/a0b500d3531032c91063fe882f6f98735f019e8985e501a993571239dce2b135.webp)

A. Connecting bar B. Insulator ? Central electrode D. Side electrode

Diagnosis steps:

![](images/3d7ce233fc0d766b30731e49e83bcd911720386c595e1aca244a3886afa99798.webp)

Next step

![](images/94cecf00a30914db7d13ac6670f1dee000864988ec41436c0fc188e7bbe61d9d.webp)

![](images/e36eacb1368d48e4a39887d78a662892883ebe92cfb737d4d72647081d4ca153.webp)

a.Check for the following troubles:

–Check the ignition coil for damage.

–Check whether the spark plug slot of the cylinder head is wet, and free of engine oil, engine coolant or water as a mandatory requirement. Complete moisture exposure of the spark plug bushing can cause arc discharge.

Next step

![](images/3582413cdee37ce532ac82f644d7dd4f21cf00bf787536256fa718bb1aba7683.webp)

Next step

![](images/7e864814c2b7dacb283b8b91c66e976d6569c16a94f7608065bba0b2b0324085.webp)

a.Check whether the spark plug torque is correct. The tightening torque of the spark plug is 20-25Nm (14.7- 18.5 lb-ft). If the torque is insufficient, the spark plug will not work properly. Excessive tightening torque may cause the insulator B to crack.
b.Check the insulator tip, not the central electrode C, for signs of leakage of electricity.
c.Check whether the side electrode D is broken or worn.
d.Check whether the central electrode C is broken, worn, or loosened by shaking the spark plug. If a click sound is heard, it means that the inside is damaged. If the central electrode C is loosened, it will reduce the spark intensity.
e.Check whether there is a bridge short circuit between electrodes C and D. The deposits on electrode C will reduce or even eliminate the gap between them.
f. Check whether the electrode is too dirty.

`geely_coolray_en_0937ec9b` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Removal procedure

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_b1d614e1` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

In the dusty area, blow around the spark plug with a long-tube air gun with the air pressure above 0.6 MPa. The long-tube air gun can go deeper into the hole. Because the four cylinder holes are half-open, the four cylinders should all be considered during the blowing process. Blow back and forth with a single cylinder blowing time of about 3 minutes (for reference, the actual cleaning of the spark plug hole shall prevail). Be sure to blow them clean.

b. Use a special tool to remove the spark plug. Special tool for spark plug: 4114870585

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_6bd491c0` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Insert the sleeve into the spark plug hole until the sleeve is fully inserted into the hexagonal face of the spark plug. Avoid damaging the spark plug due to extension rod inclination during disassembly process.

c. Remove the 4 spark plugs in turn from the cylinder head.

![](images/b5ab4ffd4623307ac9b60295bdde74e37a0978ae6eaea4e7edd0c375056033e6.webp)

Spark plug installation

a. Clean the spark plug and check the spark plug electrode gap a.
Spark plug gap: 0.6-0.7 mm

![](images/0c1dfa384c90af563460b5364e76deeebffcaa3885b86db41e17c9793147cad2.webp)

b. Insert the spark plugs in place with special tools, and then move the 4 spark plugs to the installation position in turn.

Special tool for spark plug: 4114870585 c. Use the special tool for spark plugs to turn and install the 4 spark plugs clockwise in turn.

Torque: 22.5 N m

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_1612d0de` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Use the spark plug sleeve to insert the spark plug fully into the sleeve, and then install the spark plug in the hole of the cylinder head.

The spark plug is a vulnerable part that must be scrapped and cannot be reused after falling off or bumping.

Do not install spark plugs of different suppliers on the same engine.

The angle between the axis of the spark plug mounting hole and the cylinder hole is 5.5°. When tightening, avoid the piston to be subject to lateral force.

2 Install the ignition coil.

3 Connect the negative cable of battery.

### 2.11.1.2 Starting/charging system specifications
`geely_coolray_en_6d4a677a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

![](images/fd1561e317ef3a38521d4b168b91323c33b297dc6beb663c229a755e3b5b3f80.webp)

![](images/ca919e425d3502dc7af15bf8e49599954ef35be247cd37288c2183609ba1cc05.webp)

### Warning！
`geely_coolray_en_369cb848` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:electrical | p:1

Refer to Warnings regarding battery disconnection in Warnings and Precautions

The vehicle adopts maintenance-free batteries. Compared with the traditional battery, there are no filling holes on the maintenance-free battery cover. The battery is completely sealed except for the small vents on both sides. The small amount of gas generated by the battery can be discharged through the vent holes. A small amount of gas will be generated when the electrolyte in the battery undergoes a chemical reaction. If no vent hole is provided, the pressure inside the battery will continue to increase as the gas amount increases. After the body bears the limit, the housing will break. Compared with conventional batteries, this battery has the following advantages:

– No water needs to be added during the service life of the battery.

Overcharge protection.

Risk of electricity leakage is much less than that of conventional batteries.

The weight and volume are smaller and the capacity is larger.

In the electrical system, the battery has three main functions:

Provide electric energy for the starting system when starting the vehicle.

The battery plays a pressure stabling role in the electric system of vehicles.

When the energy generated by the alternator is insufficient, the battery can provide electricity within a certain time.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_53133c0b` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

It is forbidden to disconnect the battery positive/ negative cables while the vehicle is running, which may cause damage to the vehicle's electrical equipment.

### Instructions and Operation of the Starting System
`geely_coolray_en_ef9c4e01` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The starting system mainly consists of a battery, a starting button, a body control module, an ECM, a starter, a starting relay and related lines, all of which are connected by wires. When the starting button is operated to turn the power supply mode to "ST" state, the starting relay is closed, supplying power for the magnetic switch of the starting motor, and the starting motor runs.

### Instructions and operation of the charging system
`geely_coolray_en_b65f8f15` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The charging system mainly consists of a battery, an alternator, instruments and related lines. The alternator consists of a voltage regulator, a rectifier, a stator, and a rotor, all of which are installed inside the alternator. When the engine runs, it drives the alternator to rotate through the drive belt, and the alternating current generated by it is converted into direct current through the diode rectification and sent to the charging system. The voltage regulator automatically adjusts the magnetic field current of the alternator to control the voltage output, keeping it within a suitable charging range.

Charging procedure:

a.When removing the battery from the vehicle for charging, the adapter tool kit should be installed. Make sure all charger wires are clean and firm. For best results, charge the battery when the electrolyte and polar plate are at room temperature. If the battery temperature is too low, the battery cannot be charged within a few hours after starting the charger.
b.Charge the battery until the charger indicates that the battery is fully charged or the detected battery voltage is close to full charging. The battery should be checked every half hour of charging.
c.The battery should be tested for load after charging, refer to Battery discharge current and Parasitic loading test

Charging the battery completely discharged: The following procedures must be strictly followed, otherwise a perfect battery may be replaced by mistake. The fully discharged battery must be charged according to the following procedure:

1. Use an accurate voltmeter to measure the voltages at the battery terminals. If the reading is less than 10V, the charging current will be very low, and only a few mA current can be charged into the battery after a certain period of time.

2. Set the battery charger to a higher value.

3. Continue to charge the battery and charge more than 4h at a voltage above 16V:

– If there is still no charging current when the above time is reached, the battery should be replaced.

– If the charging current is detected within the charging time, the battery is intact and can continue to be charged to a perfect state.

### 2.11.5.1 Diagnosis description
`geely_coolray_en_1e3c346a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before diagnosing the faults of the starting/charging system, refer to Instructions and Operations and System Operating Principle. Understand and be familiar with the working principle of the starting/charging system before starting a system diagnosis. This will help determine the correct fault diagnosis steps when a fault occurs, and more importantly, help determine whether the condition described by the distributor is normal operation. Any fault diagnosis of the starting/charging system should start with routine diagnosis, guiding the maintenance personnel to take the next logical step for fault diagnosis. Understanding and using the diagnosis flow chart correctly can shorten the time of diagnosis and avoid misjudgment of the faulty part.

### 2.11.5.2 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_eeb71233` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Check the after-sales installations that may affect operations of starting, charging, or ignition system to ensure that they cannot affect operations of starting, charging, or ignition system.

Check system components that are easily accessible or can be seen to find out if there is any obvious damage of the component or there is a situation that may cause a fault.

Check whether the battery is installed correctly.

– Test the state of the battery, the battery voltage should not be less than 11V. Check whether the related wires are damaged, and check whether the connections of the starter motor, starter electromagnetic switch, starting button, battery and all related grounding points are reliable.

If the battery, wires, and switches are normal, and the engine functions normally, dismount and test the starter motor.

Check the charging system: When the charging system works normally, operate the start and stop button to set the power mode to ON state, the charging indicator will turn on. When the engine starts, the charging indicator will turn off.

Check the generator to ensure that it is installed correctly and not loosened, and that the drive belt preload is normal and there is no possibility of slippage.
