### 4.4.3.1 Wheel alignment
`geely_coolray_en_4809dda1` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The driver turns the steering wheel to drive the vehicle in the desired direction. However, when driving on a straight road, the driver needs to keep operating the steering wheel to keep the vehicle driving in a straight line; or when turning a corner, it takes a lot of force to turn the vehicle, so the driver will consume a lot of physical strength and bear a lot of mental pressure. To solve the problem and prevent the early worn of the tires, the tires are installed at the vehicle (or the chassis) according to certain requirements and at certain angles. These angles are collectively known as “wheel alignment”. Alignment is a synthetic noun of angle relations between the front and rear axles, wheels, steering parts, and suspension parts.

If wheel alignment is correct, the steering will be easy. When driving in a straight line, the driver only needs to adjust the steering wheel slightly to keep it in the straight-position, and only a small amount of force is required when turning. That is to say, if all angle relationships that make up “wheel alignment” are adjusted correctly, the steering will be easy. But if any of them is not adjusted correctly, the following problems will occur: difficult steering, poor steering stability, poor steering return, and shortened tire service life.

The alignment angles of the vehicle include: toe-in, camber angles of the tires, kingpin caster angle, kingpin inclination, steering angle, included angle, thrust angle, grinding wheel radius, and others. The above angles and dimensions depend on the vehicle's suspension system, tire drive system (frontpowered front-wheel drive or front-powered rear-wheel drive, two-wheel drive or four-wheel drive), and steering system (manual or power steering). By adjusting these factors, driving performance and steering stability can achieve the optimum status. Besides, the service life of the parts can be extended.

Usually, the only angle recommended for adjustment during maintenance is the toe-in value.

1. Toe-in

![](images/41a7cffb4f28d5ad5e566d2b6474b695f31a8af5ffc902bb5a57ab4de6837598.webp)

The toe-in is used for measuring the distance of the wheels moving forward or off the center line of the vehicle. The toe-in can be understood as the comparison between the distance of the front part of two wheels and the rear part of the same wheels. If the wheels are completely parallel, the two measured values should be equivalent and the toe-in angle is zero. If the front wheels incline inward toward the center line, the toe-in angle is said to be positive. If the wheels incline outward, the toe-in angle is said to be negative. The positive and negative toe-in angles are commonly referred to as the toe-in and toe-out of the front wheels.

The toe-in is used for compensating the tendency of the tires to roll inward and outward due to the camber angle and surface resistance, so as to ensure the straight-line running of the vehicle.

### 2. Camber angle
`geely_coolray_en_2fff8b42` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

![](images/d8c1ff4549f451f6ff3f940011b63c9a524f909e964a4fd195e4eb3c9b1fc8fb.webp)

The camber angle is the angle of inclination of the tires relative to the vertical reference line. When the top of a tire inclines outward, the camber angle can be said to be positive. When the top of a tire inclines inward, the camber angle can be said to be positive. The setting of the camber angle may influence the control of the vehicle direction and tire wear.

The design of suspension and steering devices aims at reducing the tire tread wear and transferring the traction to the greatest extend by keeping the wheels perpendicular to the ground and driving in a straight line.

Inappropriate camber angle setting will cause excessive tire wear or uneven wear. Excessive positive camber angle will lead to wear on the outside wall of the tire tread. When the load on the outside wall of the tread is higher than that on the inside wall, uneven wear will occur.

Excessive negative camber angle will lead to wear on the inside wall of the tire tread. When the load on the inside wall of the tread is higher than that on the outside wall, uneven wear will occur.

3. Kingpin caster angle

![](images/40ab3e176b5700859af2b2d40231ae41a0c981043e167bedec6aad7261ade89a.webp)

After the steering is completed, the weight of the lifted body forces the steering knuckle to move down again after the steering wheel is released, so that the journal returns to the original position of driving straight ahead.

The kingpin caster angle is the angle at which the kingpin axis slopes forward or backward. The kingpin caster angle is obtained by measuring the angle between the steering axis and the vertical line by observing from the side. Inclining backward from the vertical line is called a positive kingpin caster angle, and inclining forward is called a negative kingpin caster angle. The center line of the steering axis intersects with the ground at a point, and the tire has a central point of contact with the road, the distance between these two points is called scrub radius. The kingpin caster angle can produce the stability of driving in a straight line: If the vehicle is provided with a positive kingpin caster angle, when the wheel turns to the left, the left journal tends to sink. (This is due to the fact that the journal rotates along the steering axis, and the axis is inclined.) But because the journal is fixed on the wheel assembly and the ground stops it moving downward. So the journal will not move downward, but the left steering knuckle is forced to move upward. This causes the vehicle body to rise slightly.

### 4.4.4.3 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_441a56dd` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Check after-sale fittings to ensure that they do not affect wheels and tyres.

Check system components that are easily accessible or can be seen to find out if there is any obvious damage or situation that may cause a fault; if so, repair the fault components.

Check for the following circumstances:

Obvious tire and wheel run-out. Obvious drive axle run-out. Incorrect tire pressure. Incorrect vehicle front end height.
– Wheel curve or damage.
Scarps on tires or wheels. Abnormal or excessive tire wear.

Defects in tires, including tread distortion and separation caused the collision and slight indentation of tire side wall, are normal, which do not affect the driving quality.

If the above phenomena exist, please clean, repair or replace the corresponding parts.

### 4.4.4.6 Wheel vibration diagnosis
`geely_coolray_en_42f1a7c0` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Tire dynamic balancing

Tire dynamic balancing is the easiest procedure to be checked. If the vehicle vibrates at high speeds, dynamic balance should be done first. First, double-sided dynamic balance is performed under the vehicle to correct the imbalance of the tire and wheel assemblies. The final balance on the vehicle can correct the imbalance of the brake disc or hubcap. If the balancing operation fails to eliminate the vibration at high speed, or if the vibration occurs at low speed, the run-out is probably the cause of vibration.

Run-out

Tires, wheels, or the way the wheels are connected to the vehicle can cause a run-out. To detect the possibility of a wheel runout, refer to the following wheel run-out diagnostic procedure

### 4.4.4.7 Check of wheel run-out
`geely_coolray_en_11884a32` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Use a dialgauge to measure the wheel run-out above and below the vehicle, but guarantee the installation surface is correct. Measurement both with and without tires are available. Measure the radial and end face run-out inside and outside the wheel rim flange. Fix a dial indicator beside the wheel and tire assembly, and slowly rotate the wheel for a circle to record the dialgauge reading. If the measured value is too larger and the wheel balance cannot eliminate the vibration, replace the wheel.

### 4.4.4.8 Diagnosis of the abnormal tire wear
`geely_coolray_en_05c96e77` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

There are many reasons behind the abnormal or premature tire wear, including incorrect inflation pressure, no regular tire rotation, bad driving habits or incorrect wheel alignment. If readjustment of wheel alignment is needed due to tire wear, make sure to adjust toe-in to approach zero as long as the specification is permitted.

If the following situation occurs, make transposition to tires:

Front tire wear is different from rear tire.

There is difference in wear condition of front left and front right tires.

There is difference in wear condition of rear left and rear right tires.

If the following situation occurs, check wheel alignment:

– There is difference in wear condition of front left and front right tires.
– Tread of any of front tires is worn unevenly.
– There is feather-shaped scratch on one side of the pattern strip or pattern block of front tire tread.

Several typical tire wear conditions are shown as following:

a.Eccentric wear

Reasons:

Rotating parts such as axles or bearings are faulty.
Brake system. Quick start and quick brake.
Unevenness in wheel weight and center of gravity.
There is discrepancy in size of tire and rim.

b.Feather-like wear on tire sidewall Reasons: Toe-in value is incorrect.

c.Abnormal wear Reasons: Camber is incorrect. Toe-in value is incorrect.

d.Abnormal wear

Reasons: Incorrect dynamic balance. Incorrect wheel alignment.

### 4.4.4.11 Calibration for radial tire running deviation
`geely_coolray_en_e7bffe7a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Fault definition:

In the process of driving in a straight line at a certain speed, the vehicle deviates from the original driving direction to the left or right without applying any external force to the steering wheel.

2. Criteria for judging vehicle running deviation:

– When a vehicle is running in a straight line at a certain speed, in order to maintain its original driving direction, a force is applied to the steering wheel to prevent it from rotating clockwise or counterclockwise.

When the vehicle is driving in a straight line at a certain speed, after releasing the steering wheel, the vehicle deviates from the original driving direction to the left or right (usually refers to the situation where the driving direction is 100m away from the original driving direction by more than 5m ).

### Caution

Check the front and rear wheel brakes for dragging, etc.

Check whether the tire wear degree of the same suspension differs too much.

Check that the tire pressures of the same suspension differ too much.

`geely_coolray_en_f7cd92c5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

When lifting or supporting the engine for whatever reason, do not hold the jack under the engine or any sheet metal parts. Lifting engine in an incorrect way will cause damage to the components.

### 5.2.5.1 Replacement of left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly
`geely_coolray_en_514a8b00` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Removal procedure

1 Lift the vehicle. Refer to Lifting and Jacking of Vehicle
2 Remove the left front wheel. Refer to Wheel Replacement
3 Remove the bottom fender apron of the engine. Refer to Replacement of engine bottom shield
4 Remove the left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly a. Remove the 1 fixing nut connecting the left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly with the front hub bearing assembly.

![](images/3d05d6c87829d68cf8df16b3cc5c862ec6383c890a1e17f44e9b4814e32bbaf9.webp)

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_db7068b4` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Clamp the brake disc with a straight screwdriver to prevent the brake disc from rotating. Restore the nut from the edge. Do not damage the outer ball cage thread when removing the nut.

![](images/c278421ef29a660b8ef502a48c153d115bb03bd7e83ce8ba7e88065796c8d875.webp)

b. Remove the 1 cotter pin connecting the fixing nuts of the left lower swing arm assembly of the front suspension and the left steering knuckle.

![](images/9e1f8224744fc9ce2c46cf7a8f4c84948ae3da5ab8e243f0cfcf150df7c3b5cb.webp)

c. Remove the fixing nut connecting the left lower swing arm assembly of front suspension with the left steering knuckle.

d. Use a special tool to separate the left lower swing arm assembly of the front suspension from the left steering knuckle.

Special tool: 4114720160

![](images/578fd95a20727ff38c899f2594e0032c58af5797665256c9508cdcbac5720722.webp)

e. Remove the outer end of the left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly from the left front steering knuckle.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_acfe5476` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Two persons are required to remove the outer end of the left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly.

f. Pry off the inner end of the left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly from the transmission.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_e78af045` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

When prying down the drive shaft, make the drive shaft evenly stressed and take it out. Do not damage the spline or bump the transmission housing. The drive shaft assembly should be prevented from falling, and the dust cover and oil seal should not be damaged.

Installation procedure

![](images/bd29bf6b88bbf14cbe901d8706451eaa175f915dbbd764c4a667affa16aa0110.webp)

Install the left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly a. Move the left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly to the installation position, and install the inner end of the drive shaft to the transmission.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_dfa25b57` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Prevent damage to the automatic transmission housing and oil seal end face during installation.

b. Install the outer end of the left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly to the left steering knuckle.

![](images/7db6f346236107d50c5dc7ba03a9c84f24b18aaf648384ecf5347c635450245a.webp)

![](images/595b772b68c0156e96c97273ef107462cdfcab19d3c5748a344c23b87351a7cd.webp)

c. Install and tighten the fixing nut connecting the left lower swing arm assembly of the front suspension with the left steering knuckle.

Torque: 100N·m

d. Install the 1 cotter pin connecting the front suspension left lower swing arm assembly and the left steering knuckle fixing nut.

e. Install and tighten the fixing nut connecting the left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly with the front hub bearing assembly.

Torque: 270N·m

Caution

Clamp the brake disc with a straight screwdriver to prevent the brake disc from rotating.

When installing the nuts, it is necessary to increase the edge-knocking action of the nut. The nut deformation should cling to the key slot of the outer ball cage as far as possible to prevent the nut from falling off.

2 Install the engine bottom shield.
3 Install the left front wheel.
4 Lower the vehicle.

`geely_coolray_en_4c71a420` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:transmission | p:1

When damaging and removing the differential oil seal, take care not to damage the oil seal mounting surfaces of the transmission housing and differential housing.

When removing the oil seal, some transmission oil will overflow. Pay attention to collecting the spilled oil to guide subsequent refills.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_c2589d82` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:transmission | p:1

1. During the assembly process, pay attention to the pre-applied ester on the sealing lips and do not erase it.

2. When the differential oil seal is assembled, the outer ring of the differential oil seal cannot be oiled.

3. The axial directions of the end face of the transmission differential oil seal and the standard face of the oil seal installation platform should meet the requirement of 0 mm± 0.5 mm.

2 Install the left front constant velocity drive shaft assembly.

4 Connect the negative cable of battery.

5 Refill transmission oil. Refer to Transmission oil level check procedure

### 6.1.1.1 Warnings and Precautions
`geely_coolray_en_5987d0b9` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Warning regarding the treatment of components of ESC system

Warning！

Some components of the ESC cannot be repaired in isolation. Attempts to remove or disconnect some system components can result in personal injury or abnormal operation of system. Only those components that are permitted to be removed and installed can be repaired.

Warning regarding brake dust

### Warning！
`geely_coolray_en_3c94344a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

When wheel brake components are repaired, please avoid the following operations:

a.Do not repair and grind the brake friction facing.

b.Do not sandpaper the brake friction facing.

c.Do not clean wheel brake components with a dry brush or compressed air.

Some models or brake components of after-sales installation may contain fibers that can be mixed with the dust. Inhaling fiber-containing dust can seriously damage the body. Please clean any dust on the brake components with the wet cloth.

### Warning！
`geely_coolray_en_e62768db` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

The composition of brake fluid is polyethylene glycol, which is prone to absorbing humidity and moisture. Please do not use the brake fluid in the open containers that may be contaminated with water and use improper or contaminated brake fluid, which may cause system fault, loss of control and personal injury.

### Warning！
`geely_coolray_en_ffde6205` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Brake fluid is irritating to skin and eyes. Once contacted, the following measures should be taken:

a.Eye contact flush thoroughly with water.
b. Skin contact-wash with soap and water.

Warning regarding the replacement of brake pipe

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_c75b34b6` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

When replacing the brake pipe, please install and fix it carefully and use the correct fasteners. Otherwise, it will cause damage to brake pipe and brake system, causing personal injury.

Note warning on the brake fluid filling in the brake system

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_86473141` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

When adding brake fluid to the brake master cylinder reservoir, only use brake fluid from a clean, sealed brake fluid container in compliance with Super DOT4. The use of the non-recommended brake fluid can lead to contamination and damage to rubber seals or rubber pads within hydraulic brake system components.

Precautions on the brake caliper

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_8accb470` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

When the brake caliper is removed, a steel wire should be used to hang the brake caliper to avoid damage to the brake pipe.

### 6.2.1.2 Specifications of brake system parts
`geely_coolray_en_cd4ad4fc` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

![](images/db6c8caede7a6e72c434d07019cad97af4a7186c246734f58322922b495b419c.webp)

![](images/f57efafdd0c78e2070b48ce6d5ad67b842ca550ef1374a968a76c8e3d3599dee.webp)

### 6.2.2.1 Instructions and Operations
`geely_coolray_en_187fc3be` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Composition of front disc brake system:

The front disc brake system consists of the following components:

-Brake pads: The mechanical output force generated by hydraulic brake caliper acts on the friction surface of the brake disc.

-Brake guide: Located between the disc brake pad and the brake pad mounting bracket, aiming at keeping the smooth movement of the brake pad and eliminating noise.

-Brake disc: Slow down the speed of tire and wheel assemblies using the mechanica output force applied by the disc brake pad to the friction surface of the brake disc to realize the brake of the vehicle.

-Brake caliper: Receive the fluid pressure from the brake master cylinder and convert the fluid pressure into the mechanical output force acted on the internal brake pad. In case the master cylinder returns, the brake caliper piston automatically returns.

-Brake caliper and brake pad bracket: It is used for fixing in position the disc brake pads and brake caliper. It also maintains a correct cooperative position with the hydraulic brake caliper and slides the brake pads when the mechanica output force acts on inner brake pads.

-Floating brake caliper: Used for installing the hydraulic brake caliper and fix the brake caliper in place and maintain the correct matching position with the brake caliper bracket. When there is the mechanical output force acted, the brake caliper, and the brake pad slide relatively.

Operation of the front disc brake system:

-The mechanical output force generated by hydraulic brake caliper piston acts on the internal brake pad. When the piston pushes and presses the internal brake pad outward, the brake caliper shell will pull the outer brake pad inward at the same time to evenly distribute the output force. Besides, the brake pads act on both friction surfaces of the brake disc to slow down the speed of the tire and wheel assembly. Moreover, the normal functioning of the brake pad guide and the brake caliper floating pin is very important for the even brake force distribution.

### 6.2.4.1 Check brake pads
`geely_coolray_en_cbf94b67` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Regularly check the brake pads. Take the measurements as shown below. Replace the brake pads if they are out of specification.

2. If replacement is required, the complete set of disc brake pads must be replaced according to the axle.

3. Check whether the friction surface of disc brake pads is subject to crack, break or damage.

![](images/dcabecb0db70c3f5af21c6d56e633fa064671209e85a776dee91034bebf3773c.webp)

### 6.2.4.2 Check of brake caliper
`geely_coolray_en_8efa3741` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

1. Check whether the brake caliper shell is cracked, severely worn, and damaged. If the above conditions occur, the brake caliper needs to be replaced.

2. Check whether the seal ring of the brake caliper piston dust cover is cracked, broken, chipped, aging, and not properly installed in the brake caliper body. If any of the above conditions occur, replace the brake caliper.

3. Check whether there is brake fluid leakage around the seal ring of the brake caliper piston dust cover and on the disc brake pads. If there are signs of brake fluid leakage, replace the brake caliper.

4. Check whether the brake caliper piston can enter the brake caliper cylinder smoothly and the stroke is complete. The movement of the brake caliper piston in the brake caliper cylinder should be smooth and uniform. If the brake caliper piston is catching or it is difficult to reach the bottom, the brake caliper needs to b e replaced.

### 6.2.4.3 Check of brake pad guide
`geely_coolray_en_38ab4081` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

– Check the brake pad guide for missing, serious corrosion and bending of installing projecting tongue.

– In case any above conditions is discovered, the brake pad guide needs replacement. Guarantee that the brake pads move smoothly on the disc brake pad guide without any obstruction.

### 6.2.4.4 Floating brake caliper check
`geely_coolray_en_66f94e4a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

Check whether the following conditions are in the floating brake caliper:

Catching
Stuck
– Jacket cracking or damage
Jacket missing

If any above conditions happen, the caliper and dust cover sealing ring need to be replaced.

### 6.2.4.5 Brake disc surface and wear check
`geely_coolray_en_006ca13f` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Use industrial alcohol or allowed equivalent brake cleaner to clean the friction surface of the brake disc.

2. Check whether the friction surface of brake disc suffers from the following conditions:

Serious corrosion and/or pitting
Slight surface corrosion
Cracks and/or burn spots
Serious blue discoloration
Deep scratches on the friction surface of the brake disc

In the case the friction surface of brake disc suffers from one or more above conditions, the brake disc requires surface trimming or replacement.

### 6.2.4.6 Measurement of brake disc thickness
`geely_coolray_en_51225d9e` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Clean the friction surface of brake disc with industrial alcohol or similar brake cleaner.

2. Evenly select six measuring points on one end face of the brake disc, and measure the thickness of the upper and lower end faces at the 6 points of the brake disc with an outer micrometer to obtain 6 circumferential thickness values, in addition, the distance between the micrometer and the outer edge of the brake disc must be equal during each measurement.
3. Minimum value of the six measured thickness. If the thickness of the brake disc exceeds the specification for scrapping, the brake disc needs to be replaced.
4. The maximum value of the 6 measured thicknesses minus the minimum value is the circumferential thickness difference of the brake disc. If the circumferential thickness difference of the brake disc is is too big, replace the brake discs on both sides.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_d98eb81d` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

After surface finishing or replacement of brake disc, the brake pads also require replacement.

6.2.4.7 Measurement of end face run-out value upon the assembly of brake disc

Caution

The rust or dirt of the brake disc should be removed, otherwise it may cause excessive runout of the end face of the brake disc after assembly.

1. Check the brake, control arm, shock absorber, stabilizer bar and other surrounding piece(s) for torque attenuation.

2. After cleaning the surface of the brake disc, the transmission N gear, turn the brake disc 3-5 circles by hand.

3. Contact the measuring head of the dial indicator with the friction surface of the brake disc at 90 degrees.

4. Rotate the brake disc until the dial indicator shows minimum reading, then return the dial indicator to zero.

5. Rotate the brake disc until the dial indicator shows maximum reading

6. Mark and record the end face run-out value.

7. Compare the end face run-out value upon the assembly of brake disc with the specifications.

### 6.3.2.1 Instructions and Operations
`geely_coolray_en_f749b125` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:1

Disc brake system composition:

The rear disc brake system consists of the following components:

Brake pads:

Apply the mechanical output force from the hydraulic brake caliper on the friction surface of the brake disc.

Brake pad guide:

It is located between the disc brake pad and the brake pad mounting bracket to keep the brake pad moving smoothly and eliminate noise.

Brake disc

It uses the mechanical output force of disc brake pads acting on the friction surface of the brake disc to slow down the speed of the tire and wheel assembly so as to brake the vehicle.

Brake caliper c/w EPB assembly:

It receives the liquid pressure from the brake master cylinder, converts the liquid pressure into mechanical output force acting on the inner brake pad; when the master cylinder returns, the brake caliper piston returns automatically. The brake caliper integrates an electronic parking brake EPB motor, which can be controlled by the EPB switch to realize electronic parking.

Brake caliper and brake pad support:

They are used to fix the disc brake pad and brake caliper in place, and maintain the correct matching position with the hydraulic brake caliper. When the mechanical output force acts on the inner brake pad, the brake pad slides.

Brake caliper floating pin:

It is used to install the hydraulic brake caliper, fix the brake caliper in place, and maintain the correct matching position with the brake caliper support. When there is mechanical output force, the brake caliper slides relative to the brake pad.

Rear disc brake system operation:

The mechanical output force generated by hydraulic brake caliper piston acts on the internal brake pad. When the piston pushes and presses the internal brake pad outward, the brake caliper shell will pull the outer brake pad inward at the same time to evenly distribute the output force. Besides, the brake pads act on both friction surfaces of the brake disc to slow down the speed of the tire and wheel assembly. Moreover, the normal functioning of the brake pad guide and the brake caliper floating pin is very important for the even brake force distribution.

Release EPB

When replacing the rear friction disc assembly, rear brake disc, rear EPB integrated brake caliper assembly and other parts, you need to use the diagnostic apparatus to perform the procedure of "entering maintenance mode (prepare to replace brake pads) and then perform other operations, otherwise the rear brake may be damaged; after the replacement, "exit the maintenance mode (functions performed after the replacement of brake pads)" shall be implemented.

### 6.4.2.1 Instructions and Operations
`geely_coolray_en_05ee3fa1` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Hydraulic brake system includes the following parts

Brake pedal:

Receive, enlarge, and transmit the input force of the brake system from the driver.

Brake pedal push rod:

Transmit the enlarged brake pedal input force to the vacuum booster.

Vacuum booster:

The brake system input force is enlarged through the brake pedal and transmitted by the brake pedal push rod to the vacuum booster, and applied to the hydraulic brake master pump after powered by the vacuum booster. The vacuum booster uses the vacuum source for power to reduce the control force applied by the driver to the brake pedal.

Vacuum hose:

The vacuum source that is needed for transmitting the vacuum booster.

Brake master cylinder tank:

The brake fluid used by the hydraulic brake system is provided inside.

Brake master cylinder:

Convert the mechanical input force into hydraulic output pressure, and the hydraulic output pressure is distributed to two hydraulic oil ways to supply oil for diagonal wheel brake oil way.

Brake rigid tube and brake hose:

Transfer brake fluid through the hydraulic brake system parts.

Brake cylinder:

Convert the hydraulic input pressure into a mechanical output force.

System Operation

The mechanical force from the brake pedal is converted by the master cylinder to oil pressure, after the adjustment of the hydraulic electronic control unit, and is transferred to the brake cylinder through the brake rigid tube and brake hose. The brake cylinder converts the oil pressure into the mechanical force to make the brake pad press the brake disc to conduct the brake of the vehicle.

### Brake system fault warning indicator

### 6.4.4.1 Diagnostic completed notice
`geely_coolray_en_413bb432` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

1. Be careful when replacing various parts, because it may affect the performance of the brake system and cause driving hazards. Standard parts of Geely Company should be taken.

2. When the brake system is maintained, it is very important to keep the parts and the site clean.
3. If brake fluid leakage is found, the components must be removed. If any abnormalities are found, new components should be replaced.
4. When removing the brake components, wrap the connection part of the brake pipe to prevent dust, soil, and other impurities from entering the pipe.
5. When removing or installing the brake pipe, do not damage or distort the brake pipe.
6. When installing the brake pipe or brake hose, make sure that there is no twist or bend.
7. The brake hose must be kept away from absorber oil, grease, etc.
8. After installing the brake pipe and brake hose, make sure that they do not interfere with other components.
9. Do not allow brake fluid to adhere to painted surfaces such as the vehicle body. If brake fluid leaks onto the painted surface, remove it immediately.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_3166f902` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

Air in the hydraulic brake regulator is cannot be discharged by hand. If air is mixed with ABS hydraulic brake regulator or when installing the ABS hydraulic brake regulator that is not filled with oil, the diagnostic scan tool should be used to discharge air in the brake system. When leaving the factory, ABS hydraulic brake regulator should be full of oil. After exhausting, air should not enter the ABS hydraulic brake regulator during normal maintenance procedures involving the regulator. In this case, the manual exhaust procedure should be used.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_0615926d` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Refer to Warnings and Precautions

![](images/6bdbe4fefbb3c4f0dd67663a088afd8eecea2ce5f85bfa349c0bc24b7f687b5e.webp)

1 Exhaust of hydraulic brake system

a. Keep the power in an off state. Press the brake pedal several times until the pressure in the booster is
completely removed.
b. Fill the brake fluid into the fluid reservoir. During the exhaust operation, liquid level of the fluid reservoir should be maintained over half at least.
c. Slowly depress the brake pedal to the bottom and hold.

d. Remove the bleed screw dust cover. Connect one transparent pipe to the rear bleed screw on the right rear brake clamp to immerse the pipe into the brake fluid in the transparent container. Discharge air from the right rear brake clamp in accordance with the following steps. e. Step on brake pedal slowly, do not slam on the brake pedal.

f. When pressing the brake pedal, loosen the bleed screw to discharge air from the brake clamp.
g. After the bubble escaping into the brake fluid container, fasten the rear bleed screw slightly.
h. Slowly release the brake pedal.
i. After waiting for 20s, repeat steps e to h until a ll air is discharged.
j. When loosening the bleed screw, if no more bubble
appears in the container, it indicates that all air has been discharged.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_44b982e8` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

In the exhaust process, liquid level of the total pump fluid reservoir should be maintained over half at least.

k. Tighten the bleed screws.

Torque: 12.5N·m

l. Discharge air in the remaining brake caliper in accordance with the order of left front, left rear and right front. Operate in accordance with the procedure in Steps e to I.

m. After discharging all the air in the brake caliper, check whether the brake pedal is soft. In case the pedal is soft, repeat the whole exhaust procedure until normal.

### 6.4.5.7 Replacement of vacuum pipe
`geely_coolray_en_d6a3d620` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Removal procedure

![](images/c5b07588b993fe862f6900dfad5b59e0ec2e977982020d2ced44606bee53212b.webp)

2 Disconnect the T clip A connecting the vacuum pipe with the turbocharger intake muffler.

4 Disconnect the quick-connect plug C connecting the vacuum pipe and the vacuum pump.

Installation procedure

1 Connect the quick-connect plug C connecting the vacuum pipe and the vacuum pump.
2 Connect the vacuum pipe and the vacuum booster connector B.
3 Install the clip A connecting the vacuum pipe with the turbocharger intake muffler.

4 Install the engine trim cover

### 6.5.2.1 Instructions and Operations
`geely_coolray_en_62ed704a` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

Structure and description of EPB electronic parking brake system

The parking brake control motor directly controls the rear wheel brake caliper to realize the parking brake EPB system. Its main components include the parking brake switch, the braking control unit and the parking brake actuator motor.

The parking brake switch is located on the auxiliary instrument panel behind the gearshift lever. When the parking brake switch is pulled up, the parking brake is locked. When the parking brake switch is pressed down, the parking brake is released.

The EPB system design is integrated with an independent control unit. Its main function is to receive the information from the EPB switch and the information on the CAN data bus, and then control the parking brake control motor through the processing and analysis of these information.

The parking brake control motor is installed on the left and right brake calipers of the rear wheel respectively. The motor is divided into two parts, the DC motor and the gear box, and is integrated with the rear wheel brake caliper. If any part fails, the brake caliper assembly with EPB control motor needs to be replaced, and the EPB actuator cannot be replaced separately. The control motor works during the parking braking. There is no corresponding sensor inside the control motor to detect the clamping force of the brake pads, but the clamping force can be known by the change of motor current caused by the change of load when the brake pad is meshed, and then the working condition of the DC motor is controlled by EPB control unit.

The EPB system is equipped for the parking brake through control of brake caliper. If there is a fault that the parking brake cannot be released, it is necessary to open the rear cover plate of the parking brake control motor. Then, it is proper to use a dedicated wrench to rotate the push rod in the actuating motor to release the brake caliper. After completing the operation, it is needed to use a dedicated diagnostic apparatus to reset the EPB brake caliper.

Advantages of EPB electronic parking brake system

a.The parking brake is automatically applied when the driving motor is switched off.
b.Different drivers have different power levels. Traditional parking brakes have differences in actual parking brake force. EPB brake force is stable and will not vary from person to person. It replaces the traditional parking brake

system and achieves the parking brake by simple manual switch operation. Consequently, the comfort and safety of the complete vehicle are greatly improved. c.The automatic function of auxiliary starting can be added. It occupies a small space, which makes the vehicle interior design more convenient.

Structure and description of mechanical handbrake system

The mechanical handbrake can realize the parking braking by manually operating the switch, which is mainly composed of the lever, the cable, the brake mechanism and the return spring.

The mechanical handbrake uses the mechanical transmission to perform the parking of the vehicle. The handbrake is connected with the steel wire. When the handbrake is pulled up, the steel wire will tighten the brake pad to lock the wheels to prevent the vehicle from sliding while parking.

### 6.5.3.1 System working principles
`geely_coolray_en_62bf28d3` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

When the electric parking system is operated, the power supply mode should be in ON status firstly, then the brake pedal should be stepped down and the electric parking brake switch should be instantly pushed up. At this time, the longitudinal acceleration sensor can detect the slope of the road surface and transmit the control signal to the EPB control module. The EPB control module controls the operation of the parking brake motor, thereby controlling the parking rear wheel brake caliper piston, so as to achieve the purpose of parking brake.

Electric parking system has the functions stated in the following table

![](images/d9ad32237ea89557ff719a9f6ccfd099bb0cd17834defd923b934fa3e4a813df.webp)

![](images/28e4dbfd669a753655c22fd5feb545369f66bc9b85e02c6782fa75ffd1bc55ce.webp)
The mechanical handbrake system uses the principle of leverage, and the brake mechanism can be pulled to the fixed position by the control lever to lock it by the locking teeth.

### 6.5.6.1 Diagnosis description
`geely_coolray_en_ff973a9e` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before diagnosing the fault of hydraulic brake system, refer to the description and operation, and system working principle. Understand and familiarize yourself with the working principles of hydraulic brake system before starting system diagnosis. This helps to determine the correct fault diagnosis steps when a fault occurs. More importantly, it also helps to determine whether the situation described by the distributor belongs to normal operation. Any fault diagnosis of a hydraulic brake system should start with routine inspection that guides the serviceman to take the next logical step for troubleshooting. Understand and use the diagnosis flow chart correctly to shorten the diagnosis time and avoid misjudgment of fault parts.

### 6.5.6.2 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_e1b8c55f` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

Confirm trouble symptom

The most difficult situation in trouble shooting is the absence of any symptoms. In this case, the fault described by the user must be thoroughly analyzed. The same or similar conditions and environment when the fault of the distributor’s vehicle comes out should be simulated. No matter how experienced and skilled the maintenance personnel is, if they do not confirm the symptoms of the fault, they will ignore some important things in the repair and make wrong guesses in some places. It will make trouble shooting to fail.

Check system components that are easily accessible or can be seen to find out if there is any obvious damage or there is a situation that may cause a malfunction.

The connector joints and vibration fulcrum are the main parts that should be thoroughly checked. Vibration method is recommended n case of failure due to vibration.

– Gently vibrate the potentially faulty sensor part with fingers and check for faults. Gently shake the connector in both vertical and horizontal directions. Gently shake the harness in both vertical and horizontal directions.

### 6.5.6.5 Diagnosis system
`geely_coolray_en_a7198d79` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:1

1. Description

When fault elimination of a vehicle equipped with multiplex communication on-board diagnostics (OBD) is carried out, the vehicle must be connected to an intelligent detector. Then various data output by control module can be read.

OBD specifications require the on-board computer to light up the fault lamp when faults r parts and components of system are detected. The corresponding DTC will then be recorded in control module storage. If a fault does not appear again in 3 continuous cycles, the fault lamp will go out automatically. But DTC is still recorded in control module storage.

Connect the cable of fault diagnostic apparatus to the diagnostic interface. It will operate the start and stop button to ON status. The diagnostic apparatus is then enabled. f there is a communication error on the display screen, there is a problem either in the vehicle or in the diagnostic apparatus.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_a2f6e3c5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

If communication is normal when the diagnostic apparatus is connected to another vehicle, then the diagnostic interface on the previous vehicle should be checked.

If the communication fails when the diagnostic apparatus is connected to another vehicle, then there may be a problem in the diagnostic apparatus. Please consult service department listed in the service manual of the diagnostic apparatus.

### 6.5.6.6 Read and clear of fault diagnosis code
`geely_coolray_en_ed488703` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Read DTC

a.Connect the fault diagnostic apparatus to the diagnostic interface.

b.Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "ON".

c.Read the value of DTC according to the prompts on the diagnostic apparatus screen.

2. Clear DTC

a.Connect the fault diagnostic apparatus to the fault diagnostic interface.

b.Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "ON".

c.Delete DTC according to the prompts on the diagnostic apparatus screen.

### 6.6.2.1 Instructions and Operations
`geely_coolray_en_0a308f40` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

The vehicle adopts vacuum hydraulic brake system, which is equipped with ABS anti-lock system, EBD electronic brake force distribution system, HBA brake assist system, TCS traction control system, ESC electronic body stability system, HHC hill start assist system, HDC hill descent control system, EPB electronic parking brake, AUTOHOLD automatic parking system and AEB automatic emergency brake system (some models of the vehicle configuration). It consists of hydraulic brake system, ECU, HU hydraulic control unit, wheel speed sensor and front monitoring camera. It uses the function integration control of each module system to provide higher safety, better braking performance and more flexible controllability for driving.

### Anti-lock Brake System (ABS)
`geely_coolray_en_450a78c6` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

The main function of the anti-lock braking system (ABS) is to improve the braking performance of the complete vehicle, improve the driving safety, and prevent the wheels from locking (that is, stop rolling) during the braking process, thus ensuring the driver can control the direction when braking and preventing the rear wheels from slipping. Its working principle is as follows: during emergency braking, when the wheel speed sensor installed on each wheel finds that a wheel is locked, the ABS computer immediately controls the corresponding solenoid valve to relieve the pressure of the wheel brake wheel cylinder, and the wheel resumes rotation to prevent the wheel from locking. The working process of ABS is actually a cyclic working process of "lock-release-lock-release", so that the vehicle is always in the rolling state with a critical locking clearance, effectively overcoming the vehicle deviation caused by wheel locking during emergency braking, and preventing the vehicle body from losing control.

ABS consists of the following components:

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_42b4652b` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

There is a rubber vibration isolator between the mounting bolt of the hydraulic electronic control unit and the bracket. The function of the rubber vibration isolator is to protect the hydraulic electronic control unit from the impact of vehicle vibration. The hydraulic electronic control unit cannot be decomposed and should be replaced as an assembly.

The hydraulic electronic control unit controls system functions and detects malfunctions. When the start-and-stop switch is ON and there are no ABS DTCs, the system energizes the relay to provide battery positive voltage to the solenoid and pump. The hydraulic electronic control unit continuously detects the status of the wheels and controls the slip rates of the wheels to be kept within a certain range, thereby maintaining the stability of the vehicle. The hydraulic control pipeline adopts a diagonal shunt configuration, so that the oil of the brake master cylinder flows to the left front wheel and the right rear wheel all the way, and the other oil flows to the right front wheel and the left rear wheel. Diagonal shunts are hydraulically isolated so that when one main brake circuit leaks or fails, the other can ensure continuous braking capability. The hydraulic electronic control unit includes the following main components:

– ABS control module – ABS pump and its relay Oil inlet valves, one for each wheel – Oil drain valves, one for each wheel Electromagnetic coil relay

### 2. Wheel speed sensor
`geely_coolray_en_b7f0f122` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

The wheel speed sensor is a Hall-type speed sensor, and as the wheel rotates, the ABS control module uses the wheel speed signal to calculate the wheel speed. The wheel speed sensor can be replaced separately, but the signal plate (ring gear) is embedded in the half shaft and can only be replaced together with the half shaft.

### 3. Brake lamp switch
`geely_coolray_en_f0b1dc5d` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

When the brake pedal is depressed, the brake lamp turns on, and the braking signal is sent to the ABS control module.

4. ABS warning lamp

Mounted on the instrument pack, it turns on to notify the driver of ABS fault and self-test instructions. When the system detects ABS fault, the yellow ABS fault warning lamp on the instrument will light up until the fault is eliminated. After troubleshooting, function resumes on the next ignition cycle. When the system is power-on, it will conduct self-test. The ABS warning lamp of instrument is on. If there is no fault within several seconds, it will be extinguished.

The system is automatically turned on. When the driver brakes, the system automatically monitors the slip rates of the front and rear wheels. Before the wheels are locked, the hydraulic pressure of the wheel cylinder is adjusted through the stages of pressure retention, decompression, and pressure increase, so as to keep the wheels slip rate within the specified range to prevent the wheels from locking. When the system monitors a fault, ABS function will be switched off promptly.

### Electronic Braking-force Distribution (EBD)
`geely_coolray_en_d5e9e584` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

The electronic braking force distribution system is actually an auxiliary function of ABS, which can improve the efficiency of ABS. When braking, all four brake cylinders of the vehicle will work, but due to road conditions, plus the transfer of the vehicle's center of gravity during deceleration, the grip between the four wheels and the ground will be different, and the braking force of each wheel will be different when the vehicle is unloaded and fully loaded. Under these conditions, EBD automatically monitors the grip between each wheel and the ground, reasonably distributes the braking force of the front and rear wheels, and maximizes the working efficiency of the braking system. With the assistance of the EBD system, the braking system maximizes its work efficiency, shortens the braking distance significantly, and keeps the vehicle stable when braking, improves the safety of driving, and better maintains the stability function of the vehicle when braking at corners, and increases the safety of driving at corners.

The system is automatically opened. When the driver brakes, the system automatically monitors the slip ratio of the front and rear wheels and performs calculation and comparison, reasonably distributes the braking force of the front and rear wheels, and adjusts the pipeline pressure of the front and rear wheels through the valve to maximize the braking. When the system monitors a fault, EBD function will be switched off promptly.

When EBD fails, the yellow EBD fault lamp on the instrument will light up until the fault is eliminated. After troubleshooting, function resumes on the next ignition cycle.

Brake Assist System (HBA)

The HBA system can judge the driver's braking action, increase the braking force and shorten the braking distance during emergency braking. It automatically determines whether it is an emergency braking according to the strength and speed of the driver depressing the brake pedal, and then reasonably applies an appropriate auxiliary braking force, thus providing an effective, reliable and safe braking, avoiding the driver being unable to brake in time due to the insufficient braking force applied by the driver on the brake pedal in case of emergency braking.

### Traction control system (TCS)
`geely_coolray_en_96d5e37d` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

The traction control system (TCS) is used to obtain the best traction of the vehicle under various driving conditions. The traction control module detects the speed of four wheels and the steering wheel angle sensor. When the vehicle accelerates, if the speed difference between the driving and non-driving wheels is detected to be too large, the traction control module will immediately judge that the driving force is too large, and immediately send a signal to the engine ECM to reduce the engine fuel supply and the driving force, thereby reducing the slip rate of the driving wheels. The traction control module can also understand the driver's steering intention through the steering wheel angle sensor, and then use the left and right wheel speed sensors to detect the difference in left and right wheel speeds, so as to determine whether the vehicle's steering degree is consistent with the driver's intention. If it is detected that the vehicle is understeer or oversteer, the traction control module will immediately send an order to reduce the driving force so as to realize the driver's steering intention. The traction control system can also prevent the idling of driving wheels when the vehicle runs on slippery roads such as snow, so that the vehicle can start and accelerate stably. Especially on snow-covered or muddy roads, the traction control system can well control the acceleration performance of the vehicle and prevent the vehicle from moving horizontally or drifting due to slipping of the driving wheels.

The system is automatically turned on, and the driver can turn it off through the multimedia complete vehicle setting → complete vehicle control function interface ESCSPORT switch. When the function is activated, started or accelerated, the system will automatically monitor the slip rate of the driving wheel. When it is over the set value range, through reducing the power output torque or applying hydraulic braking to the wheel, the system will prevent the wheel from skipping to reduce the lateral adhesion. When it is below the set value range, power output should be increased (not higher than the driver requirement) and the brake torque should be reduced. When the system monitors a fault, TCS will be switched off promptly. When torque needed by the driver is less than possible output torque, the intervention of TCS in power output will stop promptly.

### Electronic Stability Control System (ESC)
`geely_coolray_en_e83b8a89` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

The ESC system is a further extension of the Anti-lock Brake System (ABS) and Traction Control System (TCS) functions. The ESC can actively detect and analyze the running conditions of the vehicle and correct the driver's errors in time. The ESC is particularly sensitive to over-steer or under-steer of the vehicle. When it is found that the vehicle turns or turns too fast on a slippery road, resulting in under-steer or over-steer, the system will quickly apply brake force to single or multiple wheels when the sensor detects slippage, so as to restore the adhesion of the wheels, adjust the attitude of the vehicle when turning, and keep the vehicle on the original road, thus greatly improving the stability and safety of vehicle when turning. The system will also work together with the engine ECM. The electronic system judges that when the driving wheels slip, the intake air volume of the throttle automatically decreases, the engine speed is reduced, and the power output is reduced to brake the slipping driving wheels. In this way, slipping can be reduced and the most suitable power output between the tire and the ground grip can be maintained. At the time, no matter how the oil is supplied, the driving wheels will not slip.

The system is automatically turned on, and the driver can turn it off through the multimedia complete vehicle setting → complete vehicle control function interface ESCSPORT switch.

Hill hold control (HHC)

The hill hold control can release the brake while hill starting, and the vehicle stays in place, simplifying the operation of the hill starting. When the vehicle starts on a steep or slippery slope surface, the vehicle will slide backward during the driver's switching from the brake pedal to the accelerator pedal, which will cause difficulty in starting. In order to prevent secondary situations, the uphill auxiliary device temporarily applies braking to the four wheels to prevent the vehicle from slipping. This function effectively reduces the operation strength of the driver when the vehicle starts on a hill, so the driver can easily start the vehicle by driving and calmly operate the vehicle.

### Hill descent control (HDC)
`geely_coolray_en_a606d6e3` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Hill descent control (HDC) system refers to the automatic braking to limit the speed of the vehicle and assist the driver in going downhill without the intervention of the driver when the vehicle is going downhill. The adjustment range of speed is 8- 35 km/h. This function can be enabled through the multimedia complete vehicle setting → complete vehicle control function interface HDC switch. Only when the vehicle speed is 8-35 km/h, can the HDC switch be turned on. When going downhill, the driver can also control the downhill speed through accelerator pedal or brake pedal; System off: This function can be turned off automatically through the multimedia complete vehicle setting → complete vehicle control function interface HDC switch or when the vehicle speed is > 60 km/h.

### Automatic emergency brake system (AEB)
`geely_coolray_en_a75ef6e3` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The automatic emergency brake system monitors the distance and relative speed of the preceding target through the front monitoring camera. When a certain speed is reached, and the camera system detects a risk of collision ahead, when the driver brakes too late or the braking force is too small or there is no braking action at all, the system will take emergency braking measures to assist the driver to avoid or mitigate the collision. The alarm sensitivity can be set through the interface of multimedia setting → driving assistance → automatic emergency braking. The AEB system includes two modules: alarm and emergency braking.

1. Alarm reminder

Safe distance alarm: When the vehicle speed reaches 65 km/ h or above, the system considers that the safety distance from the preceding vehicle is too small, and reminds the driver to keep a reasonable distance through alarm.

Pre-test collision alarm: When the vehicle speed reaches 30 km/h or above, the system considers that there is potential collision risk, and will remind the driver of the potential collision risk through alarm sound, alarm picture of instrument interface, etc.

### 2. Emergency braking
`geely_coolray_en_2a0eb4ab` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Emergency brake assist: When the vehicle speed reaches 30 km/h or above, if a danger occurs, but the driver's current braking force is too small, the system will assist the driver to increase braking force to avoid or mitigate the collision.

Automatic emergency braking: When the vehicle speed reaches 5 km/h or above, when a danger occurs but the driver fails to perform effective braking, the system will intervene timely and perform automatic emergency braking to avoid or mitigate the collision.

### Electric Parking Brake (EPB)
`geely_coolray_en_5d638aef` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

The electronic parking brake (EPB) system is an electronic hand brake system that replaces the original mechanical hand brake system. It is mainly composed of an ESC control module, EPB switch, brake caliper, motor, gear sets, etc. The driver operates the EPB switch to transmit the electrical signal to the EPB module, and the ESC module drives the rear wheel caliper parking motor to work.

### AUTOHOLD
`geely_coolray_en_857c0386` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

AUTOHOLD is an intelligent brake system, which realizes the control of the four wheel brakes through the extended function of ESC and has a certain linkage relationship with the electronic parking system (EPB). When the vehicle stops temporarily and needs to be restarted in a very short time, the temporary parking in this case is completed by the brake controlled by ESC. The ESC control module measures the body level and wheel torque through its sensors, determines the vehicle sliding trend. It also applies an appropriate braking force to the wheels to keep the vehicle stationary. This braking force can just stop the vehicle from moving, so that it will not be too large, so that when you step on the accelerator again and move forward, there will be no serious forward motion. When the temporary parking exceeds a certain time limit, the brake system turns to the rear wheel parking brake (EPB is turned on) to replace the previous four wheel hydraulic brakes. When the vehicle is about to move forward, the system will detect the stepping force of the accelerator to determine whether the brake is released.

### 6.6.6.1 Diagnosis description
`geely_coolray_en_ce77b75c` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before diagnosing the system faults, refer to Instructions and Operations and system working principle. Understand and be familiar with the working principle of system, and then start system diagnosis, which helps to determine the correct fault diagnosis steps when a fault occurs. More importantly, it helps to determine whether the condition described by the customer is normal. Any fault diagnosis of system should start with a routine inspection that guides the serviceman to take the next logical step for troubleshooting. Understand and use the diagnosis flow chart correctly to shorten the diagnosis time and avoid misjudgment of fault parts.

### 6.6.6.2 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_e1b8c55f` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:1

Confirm trouble symptom

The most difficult situation in trouble shooting is the absence of any symptoms. In this case, the fault described by the user must be thoroughly analyzed. The same or similar conditions and environment when the fault of the distributor’s vehicle comes out should be simulated. No matter how experienced and skilled the maintenance personnel is, if they do not confirm the symptoms of the fault, they will ignore some important things in the repair and make wrong guesses in some places. It will make trouble shooting to fail.

Check system components that are easily accessible or can be seen to find out if there is any obvious damage or there is a situation that may cause a malfunction.

• The connector joints and vibration fulcrum are the main parts that should be thoroughly checked. Vibration method is recommended in case of failure due to vibration.

– Gently vibrate the potentially faulty sensor part with fingers and check for faults.
Gently shake the connector in both vertical and horizontal directions. Gently shake the harness in both vertical and horizontal directions.

### 6.6.6.5 Diagnosis system
`geely_coolray_en_a7198d79` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:1

1. Description

When fault elimination of a vehicle equipped with multiplex communication on-board diagnostics (OBD) is carried out, the vehicle must be connected to an intelligent detector. Then various data output by control module can be read.

OBD specifications require the on-board computer to light up the fault lamp when faults in parts and components of system are detected. The corresponding DTC will then be recorded in control module storage. If a fault does not appear again in 3 continuous cycles, the fault lamp will go out automatically. But DTC is still recorded in control module storage.

Connect the cable of fault diagnostic apparatus to the diagnostic interface. It will operate the start and stop button to ON status. The diagnostic apparatus is then enabled. If there is a communication error on the display screen, there is a problem either in the vehicle or in the diagnostic apparatus.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_a2f6e3c5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

If communication is normal when the diagnostic apparatus is connected to another vehicle, then the diagnostic interface on the previous vehicle should be checked.

If the communication fails when the diagnostic apparatus is connected to another vehicle, then there may be a problem in the diagnostic apparatus. Please consult service department listed in the service manual of the diagnostic apparatus.

### 6.6.6.6 Read and clear of fault diagnosis code
`geely_coolray_en_ed488703` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Read DTC

a.Connect the fault diagnostic apparatus to the diagnostic interface.

b.Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "ON".

c.Read the value of DTC according to the prompts on the diagnostic apparatus screen.

2. Clear DTC

a.Connect the fault diagnostic apparatus to the fault diagnostic interface.

b.Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "ON".

c.Delete DTC according to the prompts on the diagnostic apparatus screen.

C. Start the engine and run at idle speed for at least 5min.
D. Road test for at least 10min.

### 6.6.7.1 Replacement of electronic stability control module
`geely_coolray_en_f7d011cf` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

![](images/6bc98e79ff9ad41727c58d3347dc51bf37eeb4b65aad9725ade0a078fe2195f6.webp)

Removal procedure

1 Disconnect the negative cable of battery. Refer to Procedures for Disconnecting and Connecting Battery Cable
2 Lift the vehicle. Refer to Lifting and Jacking of Vehicle
3 Recycle the brake fluid. Refer to Recycle and filling of brake fluid
4 Remove engine trim cover. Refer to Replacement of engine trim cover
5 Remove the electronic stability control module a. Disconnect the harness connector of the electronic stability control module.

b. Remove the 4 fixing bolts connecting right rear No.1 brake pipe 1, left front No.1 brake pipe 2, right front No.1 brake pipe 3, and right rear No.1 brake pipe 4 with the electronic stability control module.

![](images/a655d448ebf1c5c9dd7863fa2c67ffb4b99b2ae851f5248babcfc0ccba82be05.webp)

c. Remove the 2 fixing bolts connecting No.2 brake pipe 1 and No.1 brake pipe 2 and the electronic stability control module.

d. Remove the 1 fixing nut and 1 fixing bolt connecting the ESC module and the vehicle body. e. Take off the electronic stability control module.

f. Remove the 2 fixing bolts connecting the electronic stability control module and the electronic stability control module mounting bracket. g. Take off the electronic stability control module.

### Installation procedure

### 6.7.2.1 Instructions and operations
`geely_coolray_en_978664fd` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The direct TPMS system is to install the sensor at the tire valve and the sensor can accurately detect tire pressure. The TPMS system aims to remind the driver of the under-voltage abnormality of one or more tires through the meter instrument.

### 6.7.2.2 Composition of tire pressure monitoring system
`geely_coolray_en_efb5fa68` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

TPMS system consists of the following components:

abnormal warning lamp will be maintained during the entire ignition cycle.

– TPMS control unit (integrated in BCM) TPMS sensor (one per wheel) (spare tire is not included) TPMS warning indicator

TPMS sensor

Each tire is fitted with a TPMS sensor, which is attached to the wheel rim through the tyre valve. The TPMS sensor is a battery-powered unit that periodically measures tire pressure information. Pressure information is converted into digital form by the MCU within the TPMS control unit (integrated in BCM). TPMS sensor is equipped with an RF transmission circuit for periodically transmitting information within the tire to the TPMS control unit (integrated in BCM).

### TPMS control unit (integrated in BCM)
`geely_coolray_en_17a0a6bb` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

When the vehicle ignition circuit is switched on, the MCU within the TPMS control unit and radio frequency receiving circuit start. The control unit continuously monitors wireless signals from nearby TPMS sensors. TPMS receiver unit can store the ID code (identity code, unique code that distinguishes each TPMS sensor) of the TPMS sensor. When TPMS receiver unit receives a message, it checks to see if the ID code included in the received message matches the stored ID code. If so, the TPMS receiver unit will input the information into the TPMS alarm algorithm. The algorithm evaluates the changing pressure and temperature of each tire over time and makes a decision in the event of a potentially dangerous under-pressure situation, then continuously alerts the driver through the tire pressure alarm lamp. In addition to processing the information from the TPMS sensor, the TPMS control unit can also selfcheck its circuit and operating status. If a fault is detected, the TPMS control unit will keep the TPMS fault lamp on to remind the driver of the fault of the TPMS system.

### TPMS warning lamp
`geely_coolray_en_0fb1ae63` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

When the tire pressure drops below the pressure warning level, the BCM will continuously send a signal of abnormal tire pressure. After receiving the signal of abnormal tire pressure, the instrument pack turns on the TPMS warning lamp to remind the driver to check the fault. The status of the TPMS

### 6.7.3.1 System working principles
`geely_coolray_en_0c4d07bd` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Initial mode

The four tire pressure sensor IDs are in the initial mode before they are learned, and the BCM generates a DTC of "tire pressure sensor not learned". After the four tire pressure sensors learn, the DTC is cleared.

Working mode

The four tire pressure sensors are in working mode after learning the tire pressure sensor ID.

1. In the working mode, the BCM receives positioning information and tire pressure information. BCM completes self-positioning according to the positioning information, and updates the CAN signal according to the tire pressure information.

2. In the working mode, the BCM judges and sends various faults and alarms according to the received positioning information and tire pressure information, including system fault, pressure abnormality, temperature abnormality, sensor loss, etc.

Fault priority is from high to low: system not learned, system failure (TPMS sensor signal loss, TPMS sensor failure, TPMS sensor battery low power), pressure abnormal alarm (high voltage alarm, low pressure alarm, fast leakage alarm).

TPMS system functions

Low pressure alarm: when the tire pressure is lower than 79% of the designated tire pressure (83% of the Europe Standard). The meter instrument reminds the driver to issue an low-pressure alarm.

Low pressure alarm lifting: when the tire pressure is higher than 95% of the designated tire pressure. The meter instrument lifts the low-pressure alarm.

Fast air leakage alarm: when the fast air leakage of tire is greater than 30Kpa/min, the driver is reminded to issue the fast air leakage alarm.

Fast air leakage alarm lifting: when the fast air leakage of tire is less than 30Kpa/min, the fast air leakage alarm is lifted.

### 6.7.6.1 Diagnosis description
`geely_coolray_en_7d46b026` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Before diagnosing TPMS faults, refer to Description and Operation. Understand and be familiar with the working principle of TPMS, and then start system diagnosis. This will help to confirm the correct fault diagnosis steps when a fault occurs. More importantly, it can also help to confirm whether the situation described by the customer belongs to normal operation. Any fault diagnosis of TPMS should start with a routine inspection that guides the serviceman to take the next logical step for troubleshooting. Understand and use the diagnosis flow chart correctly to shorten the diagnosis time and avoid misjudgment of fault parts.

### 6.7.6.2 Routine inspection
`geely_coolray_en_442e4d60` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Confirm customer’s fault before repair.

Check system components that are easily accessible or can be seen to find out if there is any obvious damage or there is a situation that may cause a fault.

Check whether tire pressure is normal.
Whether there are obvious mechanical or electrical damage signs.

Repair or replace the component if any faults are found.

Check the harness and harness connector to ensure that there is no sign of loosening, damage, poor contact, aging, etc.

### 6.7.6.4 Diagnosis system
`geely_coolray_en_a7198d79` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:1

1. Description

When fault elimination of a vehicle equipped with multiplex communication on-board diagnostics (OBD) is carried out, the vehicle must be connected to an intelligent detector. Then various data output by control module can be read.

OBD specifications require the on-board computer to light up the fault lamp when faults in parts and components of system are detected. The corresponding DTC will then be recorded in control module storage. If a fault does not appear again in 3 continuous cycles, the fault lamp will go out automatically. But DTC is still recorded in control module storage.

Connect the cable of fault diagnostic apparatus to the diagnostic interface. It will operate the start and stop button to ON status. The diagnostic apparatus is then enabled. If there is a communication error on the display screen, there s a problem either in the vehicle or in the diagnostic apparatus.

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_a2f6e3c5` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

If communication is normal when the diagnostic apparatus is connected to another vehicle, then the diagnostic interface on the previous vehicle should be checked.

If the communication fails when the diagnostic apparatus is connected to another vehicle, then there may be a problem in the diagnostic apparatus. Please consult service department listed in the service manual of the diagnostic apparatus.

### 6.7.6.5 Read and clear of fault diagnosis code
`geely_coolray_en_ed488703` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

1. Read DTC

a.Connect the fault diagnostic apparatus to the diagnostic interface.

b.Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "ON".

c.Read the value of DTC according to the prompts on the diagnostic apparatus screen.

2. Clear DTC

a.Connect the fault diagnostic apparatus to the fault diagnostic interface.

b.Operate the starting switch to place the power in mode "ON".

c.Delete DTC according to the prompts on the diagnostic apparatus screen.

### 6.7.6.6 Learning of sensor
`geely_coolray_en_e8fa8ced` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

The diagnostic apparatus sends the learning command with the sensor serial number through the CAN line to enter the learning state. When the sensor is triggered by the trigger tool, the TPMS control unit can receive the sensor ID accordingly. The trigger tool needs to manually trigger the TPMS sensor to send the ID. The learned ID is related to the sensor serial number. The learned ID must be related to a sensor number. In the system, the tire position corresponding to each sensor is fixed in the following order:

![](images/d34256fc2e76a4da38394daa9d213bb3bbfcbf66142abc7e30c32d8e35811447.webp)

### Caution
`geely_coolray_en_63605131` | coolray | pdf_manual | tier:4 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1

Clean the rim valve hole before installing the TPMA sensor. The contact surface between the rim valve hole and the TPMS sensor gasket shall be flat. There shall be no damage or burr on the edges of the holes on the inner and outer sides of the rim to ensure a good seal at the junction of the TPMS sensor and the rim hole.

Installation test: The tyre valve is installed and disassembled 4 times from the rim at 12 o’clock, 3 o’clock, 6 o’clock, 9 o’clock and other different directions of the rim.

Install the tyre on the rim, check the locking state of the valve core, inflate according to the tyre pressure requirements, and check the tyre valve and tightness of installation.

2 Install wheels and tires
3 Connect the negative cable of battery
4 Conduct TPMS system matching, please refer to Sensor
learning
5 Close engine compartment cover
